source.text: Καὶ εἰσελθὼν πάλιν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ δι’ ἡμερῶν ἠκούσθη ὅτι ἐν οἴκῳ ἐστίν·

records.literal_gloss: And having entered again into Capernaum after days it was heard that in [a] house he is.

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had entered Capernaum again after [some] days, it was heard that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was at home.
en.B: Some days later {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came back to Capernaum, and word got around that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was at home.
en.R: After a few days Jesus returned to the town of Capernaum. People heard that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was staying at a house there.

vi.L: Và khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại vào Ca-bê-na-um sau [mấy] ngày, người ta nghe rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang ở nhà.
vi.B: Mấy ngày sau, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trở lại Ca-bê-na-um, và người ta đồn rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang ở nhà.
vi.R: Vài ngày sau, Đức Giê-xu trở lại thị trấn Ca-bê-na-um. Người ta nghe nói {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang ở trong một ngôi nhà tại đó.

ko.L: 그리고 며칠 후에 그분이 다시 가버나움에 들어가시니, 그분이 집에 계신다는 것이 알려졌다.
ko.B: 며칠 뒤에 예수께서 다시 가버나움에 오셨다. 예수께서 집에 계신다는 소식이 퍼졌다.
ko.R: 며칠이 지나서 예수께서 다시 가버나움 마을로 돌아오셨다. 사람들은 예수께서 그곳의 한 집에 계신다는 소식을 들었다.

es.L: Y habiendo entrado de nuevo en Capernaúm después de [algunos] días, se oyó que estaba en casa.
es.B: Unos días después volvió a Capernaúm, y se corrió la voz de que estaba en casa.
es.R: Unos días después, Jesús regresó al pueblo de Capernaúm. La gente se enteró de que estaba alojado en una casa de allí.

fr.L: Et quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fut entré de nouveau dans Capharnaüm, après [quelques] jours, on apprit qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était à la maison.
fr.B: Quelques jours plus tard, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} revint à Capharnaüm, et le bruit courut qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était à la maison.
fr.R: Quelques jours après, Jésus est revenu dans la ville de Capharnaüm. Les gens ont appris qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était dans une maison de la ville.

sw.L: Na alipoingia tena Kapernaumu baada ya siku [kadhaa], ikasikika kwamba yuko nyumbani.
sw.B: Siku kadhaa baadaye alirudi Kapernaumu, na habari zikaenea kwamba yuko nyumbani.
sw.R: Baada ya siku chache Yesu alirudi katika mji wa Kapernaumu. Watu walisikia kwamba alikuwa akikaa katika nyumba moja huko.

decisions.choice: in a house: at home, most likely Simon's house (1:29)
decisions.reason: The phrase means "indoors" or "at home". Capernaum had become Jesus' base, and Simon's house is the last house named (1:29).

decisions.choice: after days: after some days
decisions.reason: The phrase gives no number. Jesus had been away preaching in the towns of Galilee (1:38-39).

decisions.choice: it was heard: people heard and passed it on
decisions.reason: The passive "it was heard" means the news spread.

decisions.choice: staying at a house there
decisions.reason: Readable does not say whose home it was, since Mark does not.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Mark 2
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change; respect for Jesus is carried at every level by "께서", "그분" and the honorific -시- ("계신다").

decisions.choice: Tenses for Mark 2: Literal keeps the Greek tenses (historic present "ils viennent", "il dit"; imperfect; passé simple for the aorists); Balanced narrates in the passé simple with the imperfect for description and the passé composé in speech; Readable uses the passé composé and imperfect throughout
decisions.reason: The French brief, recorded once for the chapter, as in Mark 1 and John. The passé simple is the normal tense of written French narrative and suits a public reading; Readable uses the past tense young readers know. Mark's historic presents are kept only at Literal.

decisions.choice: après [quelques] jours
decisions.reason: French cannot say "after days"; Literal brackets the word it needs (meaning decision m2).

source.text: καὶ συνήχθησαν πολλοὶ ὥστε μηκέτι χωρεῖν μηδὲ τὰ πρὸς τὴν θύραν, καὶ ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον.

records.literal_gloss: And were gathered many, so that no longer to have room not even the [space] at the door, and he was speaking to them the word.

en.L: And many were gathered together, so that there was no longer room, not even at the door, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was speaking the word to them.
en.B: So many people crowded in that there was no space left, even outside the door, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke the word to them.
en.R: So many people came that the house was full. There was no room left, even outside the door. Jesus was telling them God's message.

vi.L: Và nhiều người tụ họp lại, đến nỗi không còn chỗ, ngay cả ở trước cửa, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} giảng lời cho họ.
vi.B: Nhiều người tụ tập đến nỗi không còn chỗ trống, kể cả bên ngoài cửa, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} giảng đạo cho họ.
vi.R: Rất đông người kéo đến, chật cả nhà. Không còn chỗ nào trống, ngay cả bên ngoài cửa. Đức Giê-xu đang giảng sứ điệp của Đức Chúa Trời cho họ.

ko.L: 그러자 많은 사람이 모여서, 문 앞에조차 더 이상 [설] 자리가 없었다. 그리고 그분은 그들에게 말씀을 전하고 계셨다.
ko.B: 많은 사람이 모여들어, 문 밖까지도 더는 들어설 자리가 없었다. 예수께서는 그들에게 말씀을 전하셨다.
ko.R: 많은 사람이 몰려와서 집이 가득 찼다. 문 밖에도 더 설 자리가 없었다. 예수께서는 그들에게 하나님의 말씀을 전하고 계셨다.

es.L: Y se reunieron muchos, de modo que ya no había lugar ni siquiera junto a la puerta, y les hablaba la palabra.
es.B: Se juntó tanta gente que ya no cabía nadie, ni siquiera fuera, junto a la puerta; y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les anunciaba la palabra.
es.R: Llegó tanta gente que la casa se llenó. No quedaba sitio ni siquiera fuera, junto a la puerta. Jesús les enseñaba el mensaje de Dios.

fr.L: Et beaucoup [de gens] se rassemblèrent, de sorte qu’il n’y avait plus de place, pas même devant la porte, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur annonçait la parole.
fr.B: Tant de gens s’y rassemblèrent qu’il n’y avait plus de place, même devant la porte ; et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur annonçait la parole.
fr.R: Il est venu tellement de monde que la maison était pleine. Il n’y avait plus de place, même dehors devant la porte. Jésus leur annonçait le message de Dieu.

sw.L: Na wengi wakakusanyika, kiasi kwamba hapakuwa na nafasi tena, hata karibu na mlango, naye alikuwa akiwaambia neno.
sw.B: Watu wengi sana walijazana, hata hapakubaki nafasi yoyote, hata nje ya mlango, naye akawahubiria neno.
sw.R: Watu wengi sana walikuja, hata nyumba ikajaa. Hapakuwa na nafasi tena, hata nje ya mlango. Yesu alikuwa akiwaambia ujumbe wa Mungu.

decisions.choice: the word: God's message, the good news Jesus proclaimed
decisions.reason: "The word" is the message of 1:14-15. Mark uses it for Jesus' preaching (4:14, 33).

decisions.choice: not even at the door: the crowd filled the doorway and the space outside
alternatives: no one could reach the door
decisions.reason: Houses opened onto a small courtyard or the street; even that space was full, which is why the four take another way in (2:4).

decisions.choice: he was speaking: he was teaching when what follows happened
decisions.reason: The verb is continuous and sets the scene.

decisions.choice: God's message
decisions.reason: Readable says whose word it is, since "the word" alone means little to new readers.

decisions.choice: "giảng lời" (L); "giảng đạo" (B); "sứ điệp của Đức Chúa Trời" (R) for "the word"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the bare noun "lời"; "giảng đạo" is the usual Vietnamese phrase for preaching God's message, which is what the meaning decision says the word is; Readable names it, as the English Readable does. "Lời" with a capital is kept for the Word in John.

decisions.choice: "말씀" (L, B); "하나님의 말씀" (R)
decisions.reason: "the word" is God's message, the good news Jesus proclaimed (meaning decision); "말씀" is the respectful word for it, and Readable names whose word it is, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: la palabra (L, B); el mensaje de Dios (R)
decisions.reason: "La palabra" is God's message, the good news Jesus proclaimed (meaning decision m1); Readable says so.

decisions.choice: la parole (L, B); le message de Dieu (R)
decisions.reason: Here the word is God's message, the good news Jesus proclaimed (meaning decision m1), so "la parole" is right, unlike the news spread in 1:45.

source.text: καὶ ἔρχονται φέροντες πρὸς αὐτὸν παραλυτικὸν αἰρόμενον ὑπὸ τεσσάρων.

records.literal_gloss: And they come bringing to him a paralytic being carried by four.

en.L: And they come, bringing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a paralytic carried by four [men].
en.B: Then some people arrived with a paralyzed man for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, carried by four of them.
en.R: Four men came carrying a man who could not move his body. They wanted to bring him to Jesus.

vi.L: Và người ta đến, đem đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} một người bại do bốn [người] khiêng.
vi.B: Bấy giờ có mấy người đến, đem một người bại liệt đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; bốn người trong số họ khiêng anh.
vi.R: Có bốn người khiêng đến một người bị liệt, không cử động được. Họ muốn đem anh đến với Đức Giê-xu.

ko.L: 그리고 사람들이 마비된 사람 하나를 그분께 데리고 오는데, 네 [사람]이 그를 메고 있다.
ko.B: 그때 사람들이 몸이 마비된 사람 하나를 예수께 데려왔다. 네 사람이 그를 메고 왔다.
ko.R: 네 사람이 몸을 움직이지 못하는 사람 하나를 메고 왔다. 그들은 그를 예수께 데려가고 싶었다.

es.L: Y vienen trayendo hacia {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a un paralítico, llevado por cuatro.
es.B: Entonces llegaron unas personas que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} traían a un paralítico, cargado entre cuatro de ellos.
es.R: Cuatro hombres llegaron cargando a un hombre que no podía mover el cuerpo. Querían llevárselo a Jesús.

fr.L: Et ils viennent, amenant vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} un paralysé porté par quatre [hommes].
fr.B: Alors arrivèrent des gens qui {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} amenaient un paralysé ; quatre d’entre eux le portaient.
fr.R: Quatre hommes sont arrivés. Ils portaient un homme qui ne pouvait pas bouger son corps. Ils voulaient l’amener à Jésus.

sw.L: Na wanakuja wakimletea mtu aliyepooza, akibebwa na [watu] wanne.
sw.B: Kisha watu fulani wakafika wakimletea mtu aliyepooza, akiwa amebebwa na wanne kati yao.
sw.R: Watu wanne walikuja wakiwa wamembeba mtu ambaye hakuweza kusogeza mwili wake. Walitaka kumleta kwa Yesu.

decisions.choice: a paralytic: a man who could not move part or all of his body
alternatives: a man who was very weak
decisions.reason: He had to be carried on a mat (2:4).

decisions.choice: they come ... carried by four: a group, four of whom carried him
decisions.reason: "They" may be the four, or a larger group with four bearers. The faith Jesus sees (2:5) is theirs.

decisions.choice: they come: the present tense of storytelling
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense to make them vivid.

decisions.choice: four [men] (L); four men (R)
decisions.reason: "Four" in Greek is masculine, so English supplies "men".

decisions.choice: "người bại" (L); "người bại liệt" (B); "người bị liệt" (R)
decisions.reason: As in John 5:3: the short traditional word at Literal, the full modern word at Balanced, and the plain "bị liệt" with an explanation at Readable. "bất toại" is archaic.

decisions.choice: "마비된 사람" (L); "몸이 마비된 사람" (B); "몸을 움직이지 못하는 사람" (R), through Mark 2
decisions.reason: "중풍병자" is the traditional word, but today "중풍" means a stroke, which the text does not say; the Greek word names a man who could not move part or all of his body (meaning decision). The Korean of John 5:3 says "몸이 마비된 사람".

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal ("데리고 오는데", "메고 있다", "말씀하신다"); past at Balanced and Readable, through Mark 2
decisions.reason: Mark tells many past events in the present for vividness (meaning decision); Korean narrative can do the same, so Literal keeps it. One decision for the chapter.

decisions.choice: llevado por cuatro, with nothing supplied
decisions.reason: Spanish can use the number alone, as the Greek does, so Literal needs no bracketed "[hombres]".

decisions.choice: un paralysé (L, B)
decisions.reason: "Paralysé" is the everyday French word, used in the French of John 5:3; "paralytique" is older and medical. Readable describes the man, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal; past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As in chapter 1 (1:12): Literal keeps Mark's present tense of storytelling ("wanakuja", "anamwambia"), Balanced and Readable use the narrative past with -li- and -ka-. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: mtu aliyepooza (L, B); mtu ambaye hakuweza kusogeza mwili wake (R)
decisions.reason: "Kupooza" is the ordinary Swahili word for paralysis, and the relative "aliyepooza" (who was paralysed) is the plain modern way to name him; Readable describes his condition, as the English Readable does. Used through the chapter.

source.text: καὶ μὴ δυνάμενοι προσενέγκαι αὐτῷ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον ἀπεστέγασαν τὴν στέγην ὅπου ἦν, καὶ ἐξορύξαντες χαλῶσι τὸν κράβαττον ὅπου ὁ παραλυτικὸς κατέκειτο.

records.literal_gloss: And not being able to bring [him] near to him because of the crowd, they unroofed the roof where he was, and having dug [it] out they let down the mat where the paralytic was lying.

en.L: And not being able to bring [him] near to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} because of the crowd, they unroofed the roof where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was, and having dug through [it], they let down the mat on which the paralytic was lying.
en.B: The crowd kept them from getting him near Jesus, so they took off part of the roof above where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was. They broke through it and lowered the mat with the paralyzed man lying on it.
en.R: But there were too many people, and they could not get him close to Jesus. So they climbed up and made a hole in the roof above {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then they let the man down on his mat.

vi.L: Và vì không thể đem [anh] đến gần {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vì đám đông, họ dỡ mái nhà ngay trên chỗ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở, và sau khi khoét [một lỗ], họ thả chiếc chiếu mà người bại nằm trên đó xuống.
vi.B: Vì đám đông, họ không thể đưa anh đến gần Đức Giê-xu, nên họ dỡ một phần mái nhà phía trên chỗ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang ở. Họ khoét một lỗ rồi thả chiếc chiếu có người bại liệt nằm trên đó xuống.
vi.R: Nhưng người ta quá đông, nên họ không thể đưa anh đến gần Đức Giê-xu. Vì vậy, họ trèo lên mái nhà và khoét một lỗ ngay phía trên chỗ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Rồi họ thả người ấy nằm trên chiếu xuống.

ko.L: 그리고 무리 때문에 그분께 [그를] 데려갈 수 없어서, 그분이 계신 곳의 지붕을 걷어 내고 구멍을 뚫어, 마비된 사람이 누워 있는 자리를 달아 내린다.
ko.B: 사람들이 많아서 그를 예수께 데려갈 수 없었다. 그래서 그들은 예수께서 계신 곳 위의 지붕을 걷어 내고 구멍을 뚫은 다음, 몸이 마비된 사람이 누운 자리를 달아 내렸다.
ko.R: 그러나 사람들이 너무 많아서 그를 예수께 가까이 데려갈 수 없었다. 그래서 그들은 지붕 위로 올라가서, 예수께서 계신 곳 바로 위의 지붕에 구멍을 냈다. 그리고 그 사람을 자리에 눕힌 채로 달아 내렸다.

es.L: Y no pudiendo acercar[lo] a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a causa de la multitud, destecharon el techo donde estaba, y habiendo hecho una abertura, bajan la camilla en la que yacía el paralítico.
es.B: Como la multitud no les dejaba acercarlo a Jesús, quitaron parte del techo encima de donde estaba {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Abrieron un hueco y bajaron la camilla con el paralítico acostado en ella.
es.R: Pero había demasiada gente, y no podían acercarlo a Jesús. Así que subieron al techo e hicieron un agujero justo encima de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Luego bajaron al hombre en su camilla.

fr.L: Et ne pouvant pas [l’]amener jusqu’à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} à cause de la foule, ils découvrirent le toit [là] où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était, et ayant fait une ouverture, ils descendent la natte sur laquelle le paralysé était couché.
fr.B: Comme la foule les empêchait d’arriver jusqu’à Jésus, ils retirèrent une partie du toit au-dessus de l’endroit où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se trouvait. Ils y firent une ouverture et descendirent la natte sur laquelle le paralysé était couché.
fr.R: Mais il y avait trop de monde, et ils ne pouvaient pas l’amener près de Jésus. Alors ils sont montés sur le toit et ils ont fait un trou au-dessus de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Puis ils ont descendu l’homme sur sa natte.

sw.L: Na wasipoweza kumfikisha kwake kwa sababu ya umati, waliondoa paa juu ya mahali alipokuwa, na wakiisha kulitoboa, wakaushusha mkeka ambao yule aliyepooza alikuwa amelalia.
sw.B: Umati uliwazuia wasimfikishe karibu na Yesu, kwa hiyo wakaondoa sehemu ya paa juu ya mahali alipokuwa. Wakalitoboa, wakaushusha mkeka pamoja na yule mtu aliyepooza aliyekuwa amelala juu yake.
sw.R: Lakini watu walikuwa wengi mno, nao hawakuweza kumfikisha karibu na Yesu. Kwa hiyo walipanda juu ya nyumba, wakatoboa tundu katika paa juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Kisha wakamshusha yule mtu akiwa amelala juu ya mkeka wake.

decisions.choice: the roof: a flat roof of beams, branches and packed clay
decisions.reason: Houses in Galilee had flat roofs reached by an outside stair. The four could dig through the clay and branches between the beams. Luke 5:19 mentions tiles, as in houses he knew.

decisions.choice: mat: a poor person's pallet or bedroll
decisions.reason: The word is a simple mattress that a man could roll up and carry (2:11-12).

decisions.choice: bring near: bring him to Jesus
decisions.reason: The verb is used for bringing someone or something to a person. The object, the paralyzed man, is understood.

decisions.choice: climbed up
decisions.reason: Readable says how they got to the roof, which the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: "chiếu" (mat)
decisions.reason: As in John 5:8: a poor man's bedding that can be rolled up and carried; "giường" (bed) would make 2:11-12 sound impossible.

decisions.choice: "자리" for the mat, through Mark 2
decisions.reason: As John 5:8-11 in Korean: "자리" is a simple mat or bedroll, a poor man's bed (meaning decision); "침상" suggests a bed frame and "들것" a stretcher.

decisions.choice: camilla
decisions.reason: The poor man's pallet or bedroll (meaning decision m2); "camilla" is the word the Spanish of John 5:8 uses for the same Greek word.

decisions.choice: la natte
decisions.reason: A poor person's pallet or bedroll (meaning decision m2). "Natte" is the word used for the same Greek word in the French of John 5:8-11; "grabat" is old-fashioned and "brancard" suggests a stretcher with poles.

decisions.choice: [l’]amener; [là] où
decisions.reason: French needs an object for the verb and a word for the place; Literal brackets them.

decisions.choice: mkeka (mat)
decisions.reason: The word is a poor person's pallet or bedroll (meaning decision). "Mkeka" is a sleeping mat, light enough to be carried and let down; "godoro" and "kitanda" suggest a mattress or a bed frame. Used through the chapter.

source.text: καὶ ἰδὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν λέγει τῷ παραλυτικῷ· Τέκνον, ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι.

records.literal_gloss: And having seen the Jesus the faith of them he says to the paralytic, Child, are forgiven of you the sins.

en.L: And Jesus, seeing their faith, says to the paralytic, "Child, your sins are forgiven."
en.B: Jesus saw how they trusted in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the paralyzed man, "My child, your sins are forgiven."
en.R: Jesus saw that they had faith in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the man who could not move, "My child, God forgives your sins."

sw.B: Yesu alipoona imani waliyokuwa nayo {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, akamwambia yule mtu aliyepooza, "Mwanangu, dhambi zako zimesamehewa."

decisions.choice: their faith: the faith of the four and of the man himself
decisions.reason: "Their" most naturally includes those who carried him and the man they carried. Their effort showed that they trusted Jesus to help.

decisions.choice: child: a warm way to speak to someone
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks as a father or teacher would. It says nothing about the man's age.

decisions.choice: are forgiven: God forgives, and Jesus says so now
decisions.reason: The passive often means God is the one acting. Jesus declares the forgiveness as done, which the scribes take as claiming God's right (2:7).

decisions.choice: forgiveness first: the man's deepest need
alternatives: his illness was a punishment for sin
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of sins before healing. Mark does not say that the illness was caused by sin; Jesus heals and forgives as signs of the same authority (2:10-11).

decisions.choice: trusted in him (B); had faith in him (R)
decisions.reason: "Saw their faith" sounds odd in English, since faith is not seen. Balanced and Readable say what was seen. Readable keeps the key word faith.

decisions.choice: God forgives your sins
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who forgives, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: Jesus calls the man "con" ("Hỡi con" at L, "Con ơi" at B, R) and keeps "con" for "you" through 2:11
decisions.reason: The Greek word means "child" and is warm; Vietnamese says the same with "con", which also sets the relation for the rest of the scene.

decisions.choice: "đức tin" (faith) at every level
decisions.reason: The English Balanced says "trusted in him"; "đức tin" is the ordinary Vietnamese word and the key term for faith, and is plain enough for Readable, so it is kept throughout.

decisions.choice: "믿음" at every level
decisions.reason: The English Balanced says "trusted in him"; Korean keeps the noun "믿음" (faith), a key term, at every level, since it is plain enough for every reader.

decisions.choice: "아이야" (L); "얘야" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek "child" is a warm way to speak to someone (meaning decision), even to a grown man. "얘야" is the everyday warm address to a younger person; Literal keeps the noun "아이". Jesus speaks in 해라체, through Mark.

decisions.choice: la fe que tenían
decisions.reason: Spanish "fe" is an everyday word, so Balanced keeps the key term instead of the English Balanced "trusted in him".

decisions.choice: Hijo (L); Hijo mío (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is "child", used as a warm address (meaning decision m2). Spanish speaks to a younger person this way with "hijo", not "niño".

decisions.choice: leur foi (every level)
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable say "trusted" and "had faith"; French keeps the noun "foi" at every level, the same word as for faith in the letters, and Readable adds "en lui" as the English does (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Mon enfant (B, R)
decisions.reason: A warm address (meaning decision m2). "Enfant" alone sounds abrupt in French; "Mon enfant" gives the warmth, as English "My child" does.

decisions.choice: imani at every level
alternatives: walivyomwamini (B), as the English Balanced says "trusted"
decisions.reason: "Imani" is the Swahili key term for faith and reads naturally at every level here, so Balanced keeps it where the English Balanced says "trusted in him"; "kwake" (in him) says whom they trusted, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Mtoto (L); Mwanangu (B, R)
decisions.reason: The address is warm (meaning decision). "Mtoto" (child) on its own sounds like talking to a small child; "Mwanangu" (my child) is how an older person speaks kindly to a younger one in Swahili, as the English says "My child".

decisions.choice: the scribes: experts in the law of Moses
decisions.reason: As in 1:22. They are present as teachers, sitting while others stand.

decisions.choice: reasoning in their hearts: thinking it over, without saying it aloud
decisions.reason: The heart is where a person thinks and decides. They do not speak, but Jesus knows their thoughts (2:8).

decisions.choice: teachers of God's law
decisions.reason: The same words as at 1:22.

decisions.choice: "thầy thông giáo" (L, B); "thầy dạy luật" (R) for the scribes
decisions.reason: As in Mark 1:22 and John 8:3: the Protestant term, and the plainer "teachers of the law" at Readable.

decisions.choice: "율법학자" (L, B); "율법 선생" (R), through Mark
decisions.reason: As Mark 1:22 and John 8:3 in Korean: "서기관" suggests a clerk to a modern reader; these were experts in the law of Moses (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: les scribes (L, B); les spécialistes de la Loi (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 1:22 and John 8:3: Readable says what they were (meaning decision m1). The record ends with a colon, since the next sentence gives their thoughts.

decisions.choice: this one: said with contempt
decisions.reason: They do not use his name. "This one" can be scornful, as the next words show.

decisions.choice: this [man] (L); this fellow (B)
decisions.reason: Greek needs no noun; English does. Balanced keeps the scorn with "fellow".

decisions.choice: "người này" (L); "gã này" (B); "dám nói" (R); "ông ta" in 2:7b
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says "this one" is said with contempt. Vietnamese carries it in the word for the man ("gã", a slighting word) or in the verb ("dám", "dare"); the scribes do not honour Jesus with "Ngài".

decisions.choice: the scribes think about Jesus in the plain style with no honorific; "이자" (B)
decisions.reason: They speak of him with contempt (meaning decision), so Korean gives him no honorific in their words, while the narrator keeps it. "이자" (this fellow) carries the scorn at Balanced; Literal brackets the noun Korean needs after "이" (this).

decisions.choice: este (L); este individuo (B)
decisions.reason: In Spanish a bare "este" for a person sounds dismissive, as the Greek does (meaning decision m1), so Literal needs nothing supplied; Balanced makes the contempt plain.

decisions.choice: cet individu (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek "this one" is said with contempt (meaning decision m1). "Cet individu" carries the scorn in the register of a public reading; "ce type" would be too familiar.

decisions.choice: jamaa huyu (this fellow)
decisions.reason: The scribes speak with contempt (meaning decision). "Jamaa huyu" is a slighting way to refer to a man, as the English Balanced says "this fellow".

decisions.choice: blasphemes: insults God by claiming what is God's alone
decisions.reason: To blaspheme is to speak against God. They hold that Jesus takes God's place by forgiving sins. The same charge brings his death sentence (14:64).

decisions.choice: except one, God: recalls the confession that God is one
alternatives: only a way of saying alone
decisions.reason: "One" echoes the Shema, "the LORD is one" (Deuteronomy 6:4), which Jesus quotes in 12:29. Only God forgives sins (Isaiah 43:25).

decisions.choice: who is able...? a question that expects the answer: no one
decisions.reason: The question is rhetorical; they are sure no one but God can do it.

decisions.choice: He blasphemes (L); It is blasphemy (B); He is insulting God (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the verb. Readable says plainly what blaspheming is.

decisions.choice: "한 분이신 하나님" (L), "하나님 한 분" (B)

decisions.choice: in his spirit: in his own inner self
decisions.reason: "His spirit" is Jesus' own spirit, his inner life. He knows their thoughts without being told, as God does (1 Samuel 16:7).

decisions.choice: knowing: knowing fully, perceiving
decisions.reason: The verb is a strong one: he knew for certain.

decisions.choice: why...? a challenge, not a request for information
decisions.reason: Jesus goes on at once with his own question (2:9).

decisions.choice: the question, then "he asked them" (B)
alternatives: he says to them, then the question
decisions.reason: Balanced closes the quotation here, so the next question (2:9) opens its own.

decisions.choice: "tâm linh" (lowercase) for Jesus' own spirit
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads it as his own inner self, not the Holy Spirit, so the capitalised "Thánh Linh" is not used; "tâm linh" is the human spirit.

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks to the scribes as "các người"
decisions.reason: The style guide's form for Jesus speaking to opponents and crowds; also used to the Pharisees in 2:25.

decisions.choice: "Ngài hỏi họ" before the question (B)
alternatives: the question first, as the English Balanced
decisions.reason: Vietnamese introduces a quotation with a colon, so the speaker comes first.

decisions.choice: "곧" (L) for Mark's "immediately" throughout; "곧바로", "바로" as the sentence allows (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps one word for Mark's frequent "immediately" so the repetition stays visible; Balanced and Readable vary it as natural Korean does.

decisions.choice: "자신의 영으로" (L), "그 영으로" (B), "마음속으로" (R)
decisions.reason: This is Jesus' own inner self (meaning decision), not the Holy Spirit, so Korean says "영" with no honorific and never "성령"; Readable uses the plain "마음속으로".

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} corazones
decisions.reason: The possessive for plural "you" takes the reader setting with its verb: "sus" goes with ustedes, "vuestros" with vosotros.

en.R: Is it easier to tell this man, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to tell him, 'Stand up, take your mat, and walk'?

vi.L: Điều nào dễ hơn: nói với người bại: 'Tội lỗi của con được tha,' hay nói: 'Hãy đứng dậy, vác chiếu của con và bước đi'?
vi.B: Nói với người bại liệt này: 'Tội con đã được tha,' hay nói: 'Hãy đứng dậy, vác chiếu mà đi,' điều nào dễ hơn?
vi.R: Nói với người này: 'Tội con đã được tha' thì dễ hơn, hay nói: 'Hãy đứng dậy, vác chiếu và đi' thì dễ hơn?

ko.L: 어느 것이 더 쉬우냐? 마비된 사람에게 '네 죄들이 용서받는다' 하고 말하는 것이냐, 아니면 '일어나 네 자리를 들고 걸어가라' 하고 말하는 것이냐?
ko.B: 이 몸이 마비된 사람에게 '네 죄가 용서되었다'고 말하는 것과 '일어나서 네 자리를 들고 걸어가거라'고 말하는 것 가운데, 어느 쪽이 더 쉽겠느냐?
ko.R: 이 사람에게 '네 죄가 용서되었다'고 말하는 것이 쉽겠느냐, 아니면 '일어나서 네 자리를 들고 걸어가라'고 말하는 것이 쉽겠느냐?

es.L: ¿Qué es más fácil: decir al paralítico: “Tus pecados son perdonados”, o decir: “Levántate, toma tu camilla y anda”?
es.B: «¿Qué es más fácil decirle a este paralítico: “Tus pecados son perdonados”, o “Levántate, toma tu camilla y anda”?
es.R: ¿Es más fácil decirle a este hombre: “Tus pecados son perdonados”, o decirle: “Levántate, toma tu camilla y camina”?

fr.L: Qu’est-ce qui est le plus facile : dire au paralysé : “Tes péchés sont pardonnés”, ou dire : “Lève-toi, et prends ta natte, et marche” ?
fr.B: « Qu’est-ce qui est le plus facile à dire à ce paralysé : “Tes péchés sont pardonnés”, ou bien : “Lève-toi, prends ta natte et marche” ?
fr.R: Est-il plus facile de dire à cet homme : “Tes péchés sont pardonnés”, ou de lui dire : “Lève-toi, prends ta natte et marche” ?

sw.L: Ni lipi rahisi zaidi: kumwambia aliyepooza, 'Dhambi zako zinasamehewa,' au kusema, 'Inuka, uchukue mkeka wako, utembee'?
sw.B: "Ni lipi rahisi zaidi kumwambia mtu huyu aliyepooza: 'Dhambi zako zimesamehewa,' au 'Simama, chukua mkeka wako, utembee'?
sw.R: Je, ni rahisi zaidi kumwambia mtu huyu, 'Dhambi zako zimesamehewa,' au kumwambia, 'Simama, chukua mkeka wako, utembee'?

decisions.choice: which is easier? it is easier to say the words that cannot be checked
decisions.reason: Anyone can say "your sins are forgiven", since no one can see whether it happened. Saying "get up and walk" is tested at once. The healing will show that his first word was true (2:10).

decisions.choice: rise: get up
decisions.reason: The verb is the everyday word for getting up, also used of rising from death (16:6). Here the man gets up from his mat (2:12).

decisions.choice: "어느 것이 더 쉬우냐?" first, then the two sayings as questions (L)
alternatives: the two sayings first, "... 가운데 어느 것이 더 쉬우냐?" (L)
decisions.reason: Korean puts the main verb last, but Literal can keep the Greek order by asking the question first and then setting out the two options as questions; Balanced uses the ordinary Korean order.

source.text: ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ἐξουσίαν ἔχει ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας λέγει τῷ παραλυτικῷ·

records.literal_gloss: That but you may know that authority has the Son of the man on the earth to forgive sins, he says to the paralytic,

en.L: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on the earth to forgive sins"—{{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to the paralytic—
en.B: But I want you to be sure of this: the Son of Man has the right on earth to forgive sins." Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} turned to the paralyzed man.
en.R: I will show you that the Son of Man has the power here on earth to forgive sins." Then Jesus spoke to the man who could not move.

vi.L: Nhưng để các người biết rằng Con Người có thẩm quyền tha tội trên đất"—{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với người bại—
vi.B: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} muốn các người biết chắc điều này: Con Người có thẩm quyền tha tội trên đất." Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} quay sang người bại liệt.
vi.R: Ta sẽ cho các người thấy rằng Con Người có quyền tha tội ngay trên đất này." Rồi Đức Giê-xu nói với người bị liệt.

ko.L: 그러나 인자가 땅에서 죄들을 용서하는 권세를 가지고 있다는 것을 너희가 알게 하려고—" 그분이 마비된 사람에게 말씀하신다—
ko.B: 그러나 인자가 땅에서 죄를 용서하는 권세를 가지고 있다는 것을 너희에게 알게 해 주겠다." 그러고 나서 예수께서 몸이 마비된 사람에게 말씀하셨다.
ko.R: 이제 인자, 곧 사람의 아들이 이 땅에서 죄를 용서할 권세를 가지고 있다는 것을 너희에게 보여 주겠다." 그러고는 예수께서 몸을 움직이지 못하는 사람에게 말씀하셨다.

es.L: Pues para que {{plural_you:sepan|sepáis}} que el Hijo del Hombre tiene autoridad en la tierra para perdonar pecados» —dice al paralítico—:
es.B: Pues quiero que {{plural_you:sepan|sepáis}} con certeza que el Hijo del Hombre tiene autoridad en la tierra para perdonar pecados». Entonces se dirigió al paralítico.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} voy a demostrar que el Hijo del Hombre tiene poder aquí en la tierra para perdonar pecados». Entonces Jesús le habló al hombre que no podía moverse.

fr.L: Mais afin que vous sachiez que le Fils de l’homme a autorité sur la terre pour pardonner les péchés… » Il dit au paralysé :
fr.B: Eh bien, je veux que vous sachiez que le Fils de l’homme a le droit, sur la terre, de pardonner les péchés. » Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se tourna vers le paralysé.
fr.R: Je vais vous montrer que le Fils de l’homme a le pouvoir de pardonner les péchés ici, sur la terre. » Puis Jésus a parlé à l’homme qui ne pouvait pas bouger.

sw.L: Lakini ili mjue kwamba Mwana wa Adamu ana mamlaka duniani kusamehe dhambi"—anamwambia yule aliyepooza—
sw.B: Lakini nataka mjue hakika kwamba Mwana wa Adamu ana mamlaka duniani ya kusamehe dhambi." Kisha akamgeukia yule mtu aliyepooza.
sw.R: Nitawaonyesha kwamba Mwana wa Adamu ana uwezo hapa duniani wa kusamehe dhambi." Kisha Yesu akasema na yule mtu asiyeweza kusogea.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus' name for himself, recalling Daniel 7:13-14
decisions.reason: In Mark this is how Jesus speaks of himself. In Daniel 7 one like a son of man receives authority from God, which fits the claim here.

decisions.choice: authority: the right and the power
decisions.reason: The same word as in 1:22 and 1:27. Jesus claims on earth the right that the scribes say belongs to God in heaven.

decisions.choice: the sentence breaks off: Jesus stops speaking to the scribes and turns to the man
alternatives: Mark's own comment to his readers
decisions.reason: The words "he says to the paralytic" break into Jesus' sentence. Some read the first half as Mark speaking to his readers, but it most likely continues Jesus' answer to the scribes.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man, with capitals and no gender setting
decisions.reason: This is a title, as at John 1:51, so it keeps its familiar form.

decisions.choice: Then he turned to (B); Then Jesus spoke to (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable close the sentence first, so the reader is not left in a broken one.

decisions.choice: "인자" at every level; "인자, 곧 사람의 아들" once (R)
decisions.reason: "인자" is the title at every level and is never under the gender setting (style guide). Readable adds "곧 사람의 아들" once in the chapter so new readers know what the title means. Jesus speaks of himself, so the title takes no honorific in his mouth ("가지고 있다").

decisions.choice: "권세" for the authority to forgive
decisions.reason: The meaning decision gives the sense "the right and the power"; "권세" names power to act, while "권위" (1:22, 1:27) names the weight of a teacher's word.

decisions.choice: el Hijo del Hombre
decisions.reason: As in John 1:51: a title, with capitals and no gender setting. The same words at every level and throughout Mark.

decisions.choice: autoridad
decisions.reason: Spanish "autoridad" holds both the right and the power (meaning decision m2), so Balanced keeps the word of 1:22 and 1:27.

decisions.choice: pardonner les péchés… » Il dit au paralysé :
alternatives: dashes around "he says to the paralytic"
decisions.reason: The sentence breaks off as Jesus turns to the man (meaning decision m3). French shows the break with suspension points and closes the quotation; the narrator's words follow, and the next record opens Jesus's words to the man.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Adamu (for the whole of Mark)
decisions.reason: As in John 1:51: the settled Swahili title; "Adamu" is also a word for humankind (as in "binadamu"), so it keeps the sense of "son of man" in Daniel 7:13. "Mwana wa Mtu" is more literal but unfamiliar. Never under the gender setting. For review by a native speaker.

source.text: Σοὶ λέγω, ἔγειρε ἆρον τὸν κράβαττόν σου καὶ ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου.

records.literal_gloss: To you I say, rise, take up the mat of you and go to the house of you.

en.L: "To you I say, rise, take up your mat, and go to your home."
en.B: "Get up, I tell you. Take your mat and go home."
en.R: He said, "Stand up! Take your mat and go home!"

vi.L: "Ta bảo chính con: Hãy đứng dậy, vác chiếu của con và đi về nhà con."
vi.B: "Ta bảo con: Hãy đứng dậy, vác chiếu mà về nhà."
vi.R: Ngài nói: "Hãy đứng dậy! Vác chiếu của con và về nhà đi!"

ko.L: "네게 내가 말한다. 일어나 네 자리를 들고 네 집으로 가거라."
ko.B: "내가 너에게 말한다. 일어나서 네 자리를 들고 집으로 가거라."
ko.R: 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "일어나라! 네 자리를 들고 집으로 가거라!"

es.L: «A ti te digo: levántate, toma tu camilla y vete a tu casa».
es.B: «¡Levántate, te digo! Toma tu camilla y vete a casa».
es.R: Le dijo: «¡Levántate! ¡Toma tu camilla y vete a casa!».

fr.L: « À toi, je dis : lève-toi, prends ta natte et va dans ta maison. »
fr.B: « Je te l’ordonne : lève-toi, prends ta natte et rentre chez toi. »
fr.R: Il lui a dit : « Lève-toi ! Prends ta natte et rentre chez toi ! »

sw.L: "Wewe nakuambia, inuka, chukua mkeka wako, uende nyumbani kwako."
sw.B: "Simama, nakuambia. Chukua mkeka wako, uende nyumbani."
sw.R: Akasema, "Simama! Chukua mkeka wako, uende nyumbani!"

decisions.choice: to you I say: "you" stands first for emphasis
decisions.reason: After speaking to the scribes, Jesus speaks to the man himself.

decisions.choice: rise, take up, go: the command that heals
decisions.reason: The man can do what he is told only if he has been healed.

decisions.choice: "네게 내가 말한다" (L)
decisions.reason: "you" stands first in the Greek for emphasis (meaning decision); Korean word order is free enough before the verb for Literal to keep it first.

decisions.choice: Je te l’ordonne (B)
decisions.reason: "You" stands first in the Greek for emphasis (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the order; Balanced gives the weight with "ordonner", since a plain "je te le dis" sounds like a remark.

source.text: καὶ ἠγέρθη καὶ εὐθὺς ἄρας τὸν κράβαττον ἐξῆλθεν ἔμπροσθεν πάντων, ὥστε ἐξίστασθαι πάντας καὶ δοξάζειν τὸν θεὸν λέγοντας ὅτι Οὕτως οὐδέποτε εἴδομεν.

records.literal_gloss: And he rose and immediately having taken up the mat he went out before all, so that all were amazed and glorified the God saying, Thus never we saw.

en.L: And he rose, and immediately, taking up the mat, he went out in front of everyone, so that all were amazed and glorified God, saying, "We never saw [anything] like this!"
en.B: He got up, picked up his mat at once, and walked out while they all watched. They were all astonished and gave glory to God. "We have never seen anything like it!" they said.
en.R: The man got up. Right away he took his mat and went out where everyone could see him. All the people were amazed, and they praised God. They said, "We have never seen anything like this!"

vi.L: Và người ấy đứng dậy, và lập tức vác chiếu lên, đi ra trước mặt mọi người, đến nỗi tất cả đều kinh ngạc và tôn vinh Đức Chúa Trời, nói rằng: "Chúng ta chưa bao giờ thấy [điều gì] như thế này!"
vi.B: Người ấy đứng dậy, liền vác chiếu lên và đi ra trước mắt mọi người. Ai nấy đều kinh ngạc và tôn vinh Đức Chúa Trời. Họ nói: "Chúng ta chưa bao giờ thấy điều gì như vậy!"
vi.R: Người ấy đứng dậy. Ngay lập tức, anh vác chiếu lên và đi ra trước mặt mọi người. Ai cũng kinh ngạc và ngợi khen Đức Chúa Trời. Họ nói: "Chúng ta chưa bao giờ thấy chuyện như thế này!"

ko.L: 그러자 그는 일어나서 곧 자리를 들고 모든 사람 앞에서 나갔다. 그래서 모두가 놀라서 하나님께 영광을 돌리며 말했다. "우리가 이렇게 [된 것을] 결코 본 적이 없다."
ko.B: 그 사람은 일어나 곧바로 자리를 들고 모든 사람이 보는 앞에서 걸어 나갔다. 모두가 몹시 놀라 하나님께 영광을 돌리며 말했다. "우리는 이런 일을 한 번도 본 적이 없다!"
ko.R: 그 사람은 일어났다. 그리고 바로 자기 자리를 들고, 모든 사람이 보는 앞에서 걸어 나갔다. 사람들은 모두 깜짝 놀랐다. 그들은 하나님을 찬양하며 말했다. "이런 일은 처음 본다!"

es.L: Y se levantó, y enseguida, tomando la camilla, salió delante de todos, de modo que todos se asombraban y glorificaban a Dios, diciendo: «¡Nunca vimos [algo] así!».
es.B: Él se levantó, recogió enseguida su camilla y salió a la vista de todos. Todos quedaron asombrados y daban gloria a Dios. «¡Jamás hemos visto nada parecido!», decían.
es.R: El hombre se levantó. Enseguida tomó su camilla y salió, y todos lo vieron. Toda la gente estaba asombrada, y alababan a Dios. Decían: «¡Nunca hemos visto nada como esto!».

fr.L: Et il se leva, et aussitôt, ayant pris la natte, il sortit devant tous, de sorte que tous étaient hors d’eux-mêmes et glorifiaient Dieu, disant : « Jamais nous n’avons rien vu de tel ! »
fr.B: Il se leva, prit aussitôt sa natte et sortit sous les yeux de tous. Tous furent stupéfaits et rendirent gloire à Dieu en disant : « Nous n’avons jamais vu une chose pareille ! »
fr.R: L’homme s’est levé. Tout de suite, il a pris sa natte et il est sorti devant tout le monde. Tous les gens étaient très étonnés, et ils ont loué Dieu. Ils disaient : « Nous n’avons jamais vu une chose pareille ! »

sw.L: Naye akainuka, na mara moja akiuchukua mkeka, akatoka mbele ya wote, hata wote wakashangaa na kumtukuza Mungu, wakisema, "Hatujawahi kuona [kitu] kama hiki!"
sw.B: Akainuka, akauchukua mkeka wake mara moja, akatoka nje wote wakimwona. Wote walishangaa mno, wakamtukuza Mungu, wakisema, "Hatujapata kuona jambo kama hili!"
sw.R: Yule mtu akasimama. Mara moja akachukua mkeka wake, akatoka nje mahali kila mtu angeweza kumwona. Watu wote walishangaa, wakamsifu Mungu. Wakasema, "Hatujawahi kuona jambo kama hili!"

decisions.choice: went out before all: in plain sight of the crowd
decisions.reason: The crowd that blocked the door now sees him walk out through it.

decisions.choice: glorified God: praised God for what he had done
decisions.reason: The crowd gives the glory to God, whose work they see in Jesus.

decisions.choice: all: the whole crowd, perhaps the scribes too
alternatives: only the people, not the scribes
decisions.reason: Mark does not separate the scribes from the rest here.

decisions.choice: praised God
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday verb with the same meaning.

decisions.choice: inclusive "chúng ta" for the crowd's "we"
decisions.reason: The people speak among themselves, so Vietnamese uses the "we" that includes the hearers.

decisions.choice: "하나님께 영광을 돌리다" (L, B); "하나님을 찬양하다" (R)
decisions.reason: "영광을 돌리다" is the natural Korean idiom for giving God glory and keeps the key term "영광", as John 9:24 in Korean does; "영광스럽게 하다" is kept for God or Jesus glorifying. Readable says "찬양하다" (praise), as the English Readable does.

source.text: Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν πάλιν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν· καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτόν, καὶ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: And he went out again beside the sea, and all the crowd was coming to him, and he was teaching them.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out again beside the sea, and all the crowd was coming to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching them.
en.B: Once more {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out along the lakeshore. The whole crowd kept coming to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught them.
en.R: Jesus went to the shore of Lake Galilee again. A big crowd gathered around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught them.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại đi ra bờ biển; và cả đoàn dân đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} dạy dỗ họ.
vi.B: Ngài lại đi ra bờ biển. Cả đoàn dân cứ kéo đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} dạy dỗ họ.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu lại đi ra bờ biển hồ Ga-li-lê. Rất đông người kéo đến quanh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} dạy dỗ họ.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 다시 바닷가로 나가셨다. 그러자 온 무리가 그분께로 오고 있었고, 그분은 그들을 가르치고 계셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서 다시 바닷가로 나가셨다. 온 무리가 계속 예수께 몰려왔고, 예수께서는 그들을 가르치셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서 다시 갈릴리 호숫가로 가셨다. 많은 사람이 예수께 몰려왔고, 예수께서는 그들을 가르치셨다.

es.L: Y salió otra vez junto al mar; y toda la multitud venía a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y les enseñaba.
es.B: Una vez más salió a la orilla del lago. Toda la multitud acudía a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les enseñaba.
es.R: Jesús fue otra vez a la orilla del lago de Galilea. Una gran multitud se reunió a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} alrededor, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les enseñaba.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sortit de nouveau au bord de la mer ; et toute la foule venait à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les enseignait.
fr.B: Il sortit de nouveau et alla au bord du lac. Toute la foule venait à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les enseignait.
fr.R: Jésus est retourné au bord du lac de Galilée. Une grande foule s’est rassemblée autour de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a enseigné les gens.

sw.L: Naye akatoka tena kando ya bahari; na umati wote ulikuwa ukimjia, naye alikuwa akiwafundisha.
sw.B: Akatoka tena, akaenda ufuoni mwa bahari. Umati wote ukaendelea kumjia, naye akawafundisha.
sw.R: Yesu alikwenda tena ufuoni mwa Ziwa Galilaya. Umati mkubwa ukakusanyika kumzunguka, naye akawafundisha.

decisions.choice: the sea: the Sea of Galilee, a lake
decisions.reason: As in 1:16. Capernaum stood on its shore.

decisions.choice: was coming, was teaching: a stream of people and a time of teaching
decisions.reason: Both verbs are continuous.

decisions.choice: lakeshore (B); Lake Galilee (R)
decisions.reason: The Sea of Galilee is a lake, as at 1:16.

decisions.choice: "biển" (L, B); "biển hồ Ga-li-lê" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 1:16 and John 6:1: Readable names the lake and says that it is one; Literal and Balanced keep "biển".

decisions.choice: "바닷가" (L, B); "갈릴리 호숫가" (R)
decisions.reason: As 1:16: Literal and Balanced keep Mark's word "sea" for the Sea of Galilee; Readable says it is a lake and names it, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ παράγων εἶδεν Λευὶν τὸν τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον, καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἀκολούθει μοι.

records.literal_gloss: And passing by he saw Levi the [son] of the Alphaeus sitting at the tax office, and he says to him, Follow me.

en.L: And passing by, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw Levi the [son] of Alphaeus sitting at the tax office, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to him, "Follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.B: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} walked along, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} caught sight of Levi son of Alphaeus sitting in the tax office. "Follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him.
en.R: As Jesus was walking along, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw a man named Levi, the son of Alphaeus. Levi was sitting at the place where he collected taxes. Jesus said to him, "Come with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} follower."

vi.L: Và đang đi ngang qua, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy Lê-vi [con] của A-phê đang ngồi tại trạm thu thuế, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với ông: "Hãy theo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.B: Khi đi ngang qua, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy Lê-vi con A-phê đang ngồi ở trạm thu thuế. Ngài bảo ông: "Hãy theo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu đang đi dọc đường thì thấy một người tên là Lê-vi, con của A-phê. Lê-vi đang ngồi ở chỗ ông thu thuế. Đức Giê-xu nói với ông: "Hãy đến đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và làm môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."

ko.L: 그리고 지나가시다가 그분은 알패오의 [아들] 레위가 세관에 앉아 있는 것을 보시고, 그에게 말씀하신다. "나를 따라오너라."
ko.B: 예수께서 길을 가시다가, 알패오의 아들 레위가 세관에 앉아 있는 것을 보시고 말씀하셨다. "나를 따라오너라."
ko.R: 예수께서 길을 걸어가시다가 레위라는 사람을 보셨다. 그는 알패오의 아들이었다. 레위는 세금을 걷는 자리에 앉아 있었다. 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "나와 함께 가자. 나의 제자가 되어라."

es.L: Y al pasar, vio a Leví, el [hijo] de Alfeo, sentado en la oficina de impuestos, y le dice: «Sígueme».
es.B: Mientras caminaba, vio a Leví, hijo de Alfeo, sentado en su puesto de cobrador de impuestos. «Sígueme», le dijo.
es.R: Mientras Jesús caminaba, vio a un hombre llamado Leví, hijo de Alfeo. Leví estaba sentado en el lugar donde cobraba los impuestos. Jesús le dijo: «Ven conmigo y sé {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} discípulo».

fr.L: Et en passant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vit Lévi, le [fils] d’Alphée, assis au bureau des taxes, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui dit : « Suis-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. »
fr.B: En passant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} aperçut Lévi, fils d’Alphée, assis au bureau des taxes. « Suis-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} », lui dit-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}.
fr.R: Pendant que Jésus marchait, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a vu un homme appelé Lévi, le fils d’Alphée. Lévi était assis à l’endroit où il faisait payer les taxes. Jésus lui a dit : « Viens avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et deviens {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} disciple. »

sw.L: Na alipokuwa akipita, alimwona Lawi [mwana] wa Alfayo ameketi kwenye kibanda cha ushuru, naye anamwambia, "Nifuate."
sw.B: Alipokuwa akitembea, alimwona Lawi mwana wa Alfayo ameketi katika kibanda cha kutoza ushuru. Akamwambia, "Nifuate."
sw.R: Yesu alipokuwa akitembea, alimwona mtu mmoja aitwaye Lawi, mwana wa Alfayo. Lawi alikuwa ameketi mahali alipokuwa akitoza ushuru. Yesu akamwambia, "Njoo pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}}, uwe mfuasi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}."

decisions.choice: the tax office: a booth where tolls and taxes were collected
decisions.reason: Capernaum lay on a trade road near a border, and goods passing through were taxed. Collectors worked for Herod Antipas, ruler of Galilee, or for those who bought the right to collect. Many people saw them as cheats and traitors.

decisions.choice: Levi: the same man the Gospel of Matthew calls Matthew
decisions.reason: Matthew 9:9 tells the same story about a tax collector named Matthew. Mark's list of the twelve names a Matthew but no Levi (3:18), so he may have had two names.

decisions.choice: follow me: become my disciple
come with me and be my follower
decisions.reason: Readable says what following means.

decisions.choice: "Lê-vi" for Levi; "A-phê" for Alphaeus
decisions.reason: Protestant transliterations, in line with the style guide's names; neither is in its list.

decisions.choice: "세관" (L, B); "세금을 걷는 자리" (R); "레위", "알패오"
decisions.reason: "세관" is a customs or toll post, which the tax office was (meaning decision); "세무소" is a modern tax office. "레위" and "알패오" are the established Protestant spellings.

decisions.choice: Sígueme, no setting
decisions.reason: As in 1:17 and John 1:43, the pronoun for Jesus is joined to the verb and cannot take the capital. Readable's "mi" takes the setting.

decisions.choice: discípulo (R)
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "discípulo", an everyday Spanish word, as the Spanish of John does at every level; the English Readable of Mark says "follower". This applies throughout Mark.

decisions.choice: le bureau des taxes (L, B)
decisions.reason: A booth where tolls and taxes were collected (meaning decision m1). "Péage" today means a motorway toll, and "bureau des impôts" a modern tax office; "taxes" covers the duties on goods that such booths took.

decisions.choice: kibanda cha ushuru (L); kibanda cha kutoza ushuru (B)
decisions.reason: The place was a booth where tolls and taxes were collected (meaning decision). "Forodha" today means a customs post at a port or border, so Swahili describes a tax booth.

source.text: καὶ ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And having risen he followed him.

en.L: And rising, he followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: He got up and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Levi got up and went with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

vi.L: Và đứng dậy, ông đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Ông đứng dậy và đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Lê-vi đứng dậy và đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그러자 그는 일어나 그분을 따라갔다.
ko.B: 레위는 일어나 예수를 따라갔다.
ko.R: 레위는 일어나서 예수와 함께 갔다.

es.L: Y levantándose, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguió.
es.B: Él se levantó y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguió.
es.R: Leví se levantó y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguió.

fr.L: Et s’étant levé, il {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivit.
fr.B: Il se leva et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivit.
fr.R: Lévi s’est levé et il est parti avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Naye akiinuka, akamfuata.
sw.B: Akasimama, akamfuata.
sw.R: Lawi akasimama, akaenda pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.

decisions.choice: rising, he followed: he left his work at once
decisions.reason: Like the fishermen (1:18), he leaves his trade at a word.

source.text: Καὶ γίνεται κατακεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ, καὶ πολλοὶ τελῶναι καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ συνανέκειντο τῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ, ἦσαν γὰρ πολλοὶ καὶ ἠκολούθουν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And it comes to pass him to recline in the house of him, and many tax collectors and sinners were reclining with the Jesus and the disciples of him; there were for many, and they were following him.

en.L: And it happens that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is reclining at table in his house, and many tax collectors and sinners were reclining with Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, for there were many, and they were following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Later Jesus was having a meal in Levi's house, and many tax collectors and sinners shared the table with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples. There were many such people among those who followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Later Jesus ate a meal at Levi's house. Many tax collectors and other people known as sinners ate there with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers. Many people like that were following Jesus.

vi.L: Và xảy ra là {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngả mình dùng bữa trong nhà ông, và nhiều người thu thuế và người tội lỗi cùng ngả mình dùng bữa với Đức Giê-xu và các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì có nhiều người [như vậy], và họ đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Sau đó, Đức Giê-xu dùng bữa tại nhà Lê-vi. Nhiều người thu thuế và người tội lỗi cùng ngồi ăn với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì trong số những người đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có nhiều người như thế.
vi.R: Sau đó, Đức Giê-xu ăn một bữa tại nhà Lê-vi. Nhiều người thu thuế và những người khác bị coi là tội lỗi cũng ăn với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Có rất nhiều người như vậy đi theo Đức Giê-xu.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 그의 집에서 [식탁에] 기대어 앉아 계시게 된다. 그런데 많은 세리와 죄인이 예수와 그분의 제자들과 함께 기대어 앉아 있었다. 그런 사람이 많았고, 그들이 그분을 따르고 있었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그 뒤에 예수께서 레위의 집에서 식사를 하고 계셨는데, 많은 세리와 죄인이 예수와 제자들과 함께 식탁에 앉아 있었다. 예수를 따르는 사람들 가운데 그런 사람이 많았던 것이다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 예수께서 레위의 집에서 식사를 하셨다. 많은 세금 걷는 사람들과, 죄인이라고 손가락질받던 사람들이 예수와 제자들과 함께 음식을 먹었다. 그런 사람들 가운데 많은 이가 예수를 따르고 있었다.

es.L: Y sucede que está recostado a la mesa en su casa, y muchos recaudadores de impuestos y pecadores estaban a la mesa con Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, porque eran muchos, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} seguían.
es.B: Más tarde, Jesús estaba comiendo en casa de Leví, y muchos recaudadores de impuestos y pecadores compartían la mesa con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, pues había muchos de ellos entre los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} seguían.
es.R: Más tarde, Jesús fue a comer a la casa de Leví. Muchos recaudadores de impuestos y otras personas a las que llamaban pecadores comieron allí con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos. Mucha gente así seguía a Jesús.

fr.L: Et il arrive qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se trouve à table dans sa maison, et beaucoup de collecteurs d’impôts et de pécheurs étaient à table avec Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples ; car ils étaient nombreux, et ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivaient.
fr.B: Plus tard, Jésus prenait un repas dans la maison de Lévi, et beaucoup de collecteurs d’impôts et de pécheurs étaient à table avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples. Il y avait en effet beaucoup de gens de cette sorte parmi ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivaient.
fr.R: Plus tard, Jésus a mangé chez Lévi. Beaucoup de collecteurs d’impôts et d’autres personnes qu’on appelait des pécheurs mangeaient là avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples. Beaucoup de gens comme eux suivaient Jésus.

sw.L: Na inatokea kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anaketi chakulani nyumbani mwake, na watoza ushuru wengi na wenye dhambi walikuwa wameketi pamoja na Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}; kwa maana walikuwa wengi, nao walikuwa wakimfuata.
sw.B: Baadaye Yesu alikuwa akila chakula nyumbani kwa Lawi, na watoza ushuru wengi na wenye dhambi walikula pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Watu wa namna hiyo walikuwa wengi miongoni mwa wale waliomfuata.
sw.R: Baadaye Yesu alikula chakula nyumbani kwa Lawi. Watoza ushuru wengi na watu wengine waliojulikana kuwa wenye dhambi walikula pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Watu wengi wa namna hiyo walikuwa wakimfuata Yesu.

decisions.choice: his house: Levi's house
decisions.reason: "His" could be Jesus or Levi. Luke 5:29 says Levi gave a great feast in his house, which fits the call that comes just before.

decisions.choice: reclining: lying on couches at a meal
decisions.reason: At a formal meal guests lay on their sides around a low table. Eating together meant friendship and acceptance.

decisions.choice: sinners: people known for breaking the law, or who did not keep it as the Pharisees taught
decisions.reason: The word marks people that religious Jews kept away from: those with a bad name, and those careless of the law's purity rules.

decisions.choice: there were many, and they followed him: many such people were among his followers
alternatives: there were many disciples, who followed him
decisions.reason: The Greek can mean that many tax collectors and sinners followed Jesus, or that his disciples were many. This is the first time Mark uses the word disciples.

decisions.choice: Levi's house
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the house's owner, following the meaning note.

decisions.choice: other people known as sinners
decisions.reason: Readable shows that "sinners" is a label others gave them.

decisions.choice: "ngả mình dùng bữa" (L); "dùng bữa", "ngồi ăn" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Guests lay on couches at a meal (meaning decision); Literal shows the posture, Balanced and Readable use the ordinary Vietnamese words for eating together.

decisions.choice: "môn đồ" at Readable too
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "followers"; the style guide keeps "môn đồ" at every level, as in John, because it is the ordinary church word and recurs through the Gospel.

decisions.choice: "세리" (L, B), "세금 걷는 사람" (R); "죄인" at every level
decisions.reason: "세리" is the established word but is not everyday Korean, so Readable says what these men did. "죄인" keeps the word the Pharisees used of people known for breaking the law (meaning decision); Readable adds that others pointed at them, as the English Readable adds "known as".

decisions.choice: "[식탁에] 기대어 앉아" (L), "식탁에 앉아" (B), "음식을 먹었다" (R); "제자들" at every level
decisions.reason: Guests lay on couches at a meal (meaning decision); "기대어 앉다" gives that picture without suggesting lying in bed, and Literal brackets the table Korean needs. As in John in Korean, "제자" stays at Readable where the English says "followers", since it is an everyday word for a teacher's pupils.

decisions.choice: recaudadores de impuestos
decisions.reason: Says plainly who they were; "publicanos", the traditional word, is no longer understood by most readers. Throughout Mark.

decisions.choice: está recostado a la mesa en su casa
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Mark's present tense and his "his house" without a span, since meaning decision m1 takes it as Levi's house; guests lay on couches at a meal (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: les collecteurs d’impôts (every level), for the whole book
decisions.reason: "Publicain", the traditional French Bible word, no longer tells a reader what these men did; "collecteur d’impôts" says it plainly at every level.

decisions.choice: ses disciples (R)
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "followers". French keeps "disciples" at every level, Readable included, as the French brief does for John: the word is plain enough in French and recurs through the Gospel.

decisions.choice: se trouve à table, étaient à table (L)
decisions.reason: Guests lay on couches at such a meal (meaning decision m2); "être à table" is the French for taking part in a meal, and "allongé" would puzzle readers without saying more.

decisions.choice: watoza ushuru; wenye dhambi
decisions.reason: "Watoza ushuru" is the established Swahili name for the tax collectors; "wenye dhambi" (sinners) is the word used for sinners in the letters. Used through Mark.

decisions.choice: wanafunzi at Readable too
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "followers". Swahili "wanafunzi" (disciples, learners) is plain enough for every reader, and the Swahili style guide keeps it at every level, as in John; "wafuasi" is kept for those who follow him in a looser sense. Used through Mark.

source.text: καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς τῶν Φαρισαίων ἰδόντες ὅτι ἐσθίει μετὰ τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν καὶ τελωνῶν ἔλεγον τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Ὅτι μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίει;

records.literal_gloss: And the scribes of the Pharisees having seen that he eats with the sinners and tax collectors were saying to the disciples of him, Why with the tax collectors and sinners does he eat?

en.L: And the scribes of the Pharisees, seeing that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was eating with the sinners and tax collectors, were saying to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Why does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} eat with the tax collectors and sinners?"
en.B: Some scribes who were Pharisees saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} eating with sinners and tax collectors, and they asked {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Why is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} eating with tax collectors and sinners?"
en.R: Some teachers of God's law who were Pharisees saw this. They asked {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, "Why does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} share meals with tax collectors and sinners?"

vi.L: Và các thầy thông giáo thuộc phái Pha-ri-si, thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ăn với những người tội lỗi và người thu thuế, thì nói với các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Sao ông ta ăn với người thu thuế và người tội lỗi?"
vi.B: Mấy thầy thông giáo thuộc phái Pha-ri-si thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ăn với người tội lỗi và người thu thuế thì hỏi các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Sao ông ta lại ăn chung với người thu thuế và người tội lỗi?"
vi.R: Mấy thầy dạy luật thuộc nhóm Pha-ri-si thấy vậy. Họ hỏi các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Sao ông ta lại ăn uống chung với người thu thuế và người tội lỗi?"

ko.L: 그리고 바리새파의 율법학자들은 그분이 죄인들과 세리들과 함께 잡수시는 것을 보고, 그분의 제자들에게 말하고 있었다. "어찌하여 그는 세리들과 죄인들과 함께 먹느냐?"
ko.B: 바리새파에 속한 율법학자들이 예수께서 죄인들과 세리들과 함께 잡수시는 것을 보고, 그분의 제자들에게 물었다. "그는 왜 세리들과 죄인들과 함께 먹느냐?"
ko.R: 바리새파 사람인 율법 선생 몇 명이 그것을 보았다. 그들이 예수의 제자들에게 물었다. "그 사람은 왜 세금 걷는 사람들이나 죄인들과 함께 밥을 먹느냐?"

es.L: Y los escribas de los fariseos, viendo que comía con los pecadores y recaudadores de impuestos, decían a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «¿Por qué come con los recaudadores de impuestos y pecadores?».
es.B: Algunos escribas que eran fariseos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vieron comer con pecadores y recaudadores de impuestos, y preguntaron a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «¿Por qué come con recaudadores de impuestos y pecadores?».
es.R: Algunos maestros de la ley de Dios que eran fariseos vieron esto. Les preguntaron a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «¿Por qué comparte la mesa con recaudadores de impuestos y pecadores?».

fr.L: Et les scribes des Pharisiens, voyant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} mangeait avec les pécheurs et les collecteurs d’impôts, disaient à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples : « Pourquoi mange-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avec les collecteurs d’impôts et les pécheurs ? »
fr.B: Des scribes du parti des Pharisiens {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} virent manger avec des pécheurs et des collecteurs d’impôts, et ils demandèrent à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples : « Pourquoi mange-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avec les collecteurs d’impôts et les pécheurs ? »
fr.R: Des spécialistes de la Loi qui étaient des Pharisiens ont vu cela. Ils ont demandé à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples : « Pourquoi est-ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} partage des repas avec des collecteurs d’impôts et des pécheurs ? »

sw.L: Na waandishi wa Mafarisayo, walipoona kwamba anakula pamoja na wenye dhambi na watoza ushuru, walikuwa wakiwaambia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, "Mbona anakula pamoja na watoza ushuru na wenye dhambi?"
sw.B: Baadhi ya waandishi waliokuwa Mafarisayo walimwona akila pamoja na wenye dhambi na watoza ushuru, wakawauliza wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, "Kwa nini anakula pamoja na watoza ushuru na wenye dhambi?"
sw.R: Baadhi ya walimu wa Sheria waliokuwa Mafarisayo waliona hayo. Wakawauliza wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, "Kwa nini anashiriki chakula pamoja na watoza ushuru na wenye dhambi?"

decisions.choice: the scribes of the Pharisees: scribes who belonged to the Pharisees
decisions.reason: The Pharisees were a movement devoted to keeping the law exactly, including rules of purity at meals. Some scribes belonged to them.

decisions.choice: a question: why does he eat with them?
alternatives: a statement: he eats with tax collectors and sinners!
decisions.reason: The Greek word that opens the saying can introduce a question or a statement. The SBLGNT punctuates it as a question.

decisions.choice: eating with them: sharing a meal meant accepting them
alternatives: only being in the same room
decisions.reason: To the Pharisees, eating with such people made a teacher unclean and approved their way of life.

decisions.choice: teachers of God's law
decisions.reason: The same words as at 1:22.

decisions.choice: "ông ta" in the scribes' question, with no setting span
decisions.reason: The style guide has opponents speak of Jesus as "ông ta"; the English deity_pronoun span has no counterpart, since the speakers do not honour him.

decisions.choice: the scribes speak to the disciples in 해라체 and of Jesus with no honorific ("그는 ... 먹느냐?"); the narrator says "잡수시는"
decisions.reason: Teachers of the law address a rival teacher's disciples as inferiors, and their disapproval shows in giving Jesus no honorific; the narrator keeps the honorific for Jesus throughout.

source.text: καὶ ἀκούσας ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς ὅτι Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ἰσχύοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλ’ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες· οὐκ ἦλθον καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλούς.

records.literal_gloss: And having heard the Jesus says to them, Not need have the [ones] being strong of a physician but the [ones] badly having; not I came to call righteous but sinners.

en.L: And hearing [this], Jesus says to them, "Those who are strong have no need of a physician, but those who are sick; I did not come to call righteous [people], but sinners."
en.B: Jesus heard it and told them, "People who are well do not need a doctor; sick people do. I came to call sinners, not the righteous."
en.R: Jesus heard what they said. He told them, "Healthy people do not need a doctor. Sick people do. I did not come to invite good people. I came to invite sinners."

vi.L: Và nghe [vậy], Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Người mạnh khỏe không cần thầy thuốc, nhưng người đau ốm [mới cần]; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã không đến để gọi người công chính, nhưng [để gọi] người tội lỗi."
vi.B: Nghe vậy, Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Người khỏe mạnh không cần thầy thuốc, người đau ốm mới cần. Ta đến không phải để kêu gọi người công chính, mà để kêu gọi người tội lỗi."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nghe họ nói vậy. Ngài bảo họ: "Người khỏe thì không cần bác sĩ. Người bệnh mới cần. Ta không đến để mời người tốt. Ta đến để mời người tội lỗi."

ko.L: 그리고 예수께서 들으시고 그들에게 말씀하신다. "힘센 이들에게는 의사가 필요 없다. 오히려 몸이 좋지 않은 이들에게 [필요하다]. 내가 온 것은 의인들을 부르기 위해서가 아니라 죄인들을 [부르기 위해서다]."
ko.B: 예수께서 그 말을 들으시고 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "몸이 성한 사람에게는 의사가 필요 없다. 의사가 필요한 사람은 아픈 사람이다. 내가 온 것은 의인들이 아니라 죄인들을 부르기 위해서다."
ko.R: 예수께서 그들의 말을 들으셨다. 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "건강한 사람은 의사를 찾지 않는다. 아픈 사람이 의사를 찾는다. 나는 착한 사람들을 초대하러 오지 않았다. 죄인들을 초대하러 왔다."

es.L: Y al oír[lo], Jesús les dice: «No tienen necesidad de médico los que están fuertes, sino los que están enfermos; no vine a llamar a justos, sino a pecadores».
es.B: Jesús lo oyó y les dijo: «Los sanos no necesitan médico, sino los enfermos. No he venido a llamar a justos, sino a pecadores».
es.R: Jesús oyó lo que decían. Les dijo: «Las personas sanas no necesitan médico. Los enfermos sí lo necesitan. Yo no vine a invitar a la gente buena. Vine a invitar a los pecadores».

fr.L: Et ayant entendu [cela], Jésus leur dit : « Ceux qui sont en force n’ont pas besoin de médecin, mais ceux qui vont mal ; je ne suis pas venu appeler des justes, mais des pécheurs. »
fr.B: Jésus l’entendit et leur dit : « Les bien-portants n’ont pas besoin du médecin ; ce sont les malades qui en ont besoin. Je suis venu appeler les pécheurs, pas les justes. »
fr.R: Jésus a entendu ce qu’ils disaient. Il leur a dit : « Les gens en bonne santé n’ont pas besoin de médecin. Ce sont les malades qui en ont besoin. Je ne suis pas venu inviter les gens bien. Je suis venu inviter les pécheurs. »

sw.L: Na Yesu aliposikia, anawaambia, "Wenye nguvu hawana haja ya tabibu, bali walio wagonjwa; sikuja kuwaita [watu] wenye haki, ila wenye dhambi."
sw.B: Yesu aliposikia hayo, akawaambia, "Watu walio wazima hawahitaji daktari; wagonjwa ndio wanaomhitaji. Nimekuja kuwaita wenye dhambi, si wenye haki."
sw.R: Yesu alisikia waliyosema. Akawaambia, "Watu wenye afya hawahitaji daktari. Wagonjwa ndio wanaomhitaji. Sikuja kuwaalika watu wema. Nimekuja kuwaalika wenye dhambi."

decisions.choice: the strong do not need a physician: a common saying
decisions.reason: Jesus uses a proverb: a doctor goes where the sick are. So he goes to sinners.

decisions.choice: to call: to invite, as to a meal, and to summon to the kingdom
decisions.reason: The word is used for inviting guests to a feast and for Jesus' call to follow him (1:20).

decisions.choice: the righteous: those who think themselves right with God, or are thought so
alternatives: people who truly need nothing from God
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks in the scribes' own terms. He does not say there are people who need no repentance.

decisions.choice: good people
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for those who were counted righteous.

decisions.choice: "부르다" (L, B); "초대하다" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means both to invite, as to a meal, and to summon to the kingdom (meaning decision); "부르다" covers both in Korean, and Readable chooses "초대하다" (invite), which fits the meal at Levi's house, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: llamar (L, B); invitar (R)
decisions.reason: "Llamar" can mean both inviting to a meal and summoning (meaning decision m2), as in 1:20; Readable says "invitar" as the English does.

decisions.choice: les gens bien (R)
decisions.reason: As the English Readable says "good people": those who think themselves right with God, or are thought so (meaning decision m3). "Les gens bien" is the everyday French for respectable people.

decisions.choice: tabibu (L); daktari (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Tabibu" is the older word for a healer and suits the ancient saying at Literal; "daktari" is the everyday word, as the English moves from "physician" to "doctor".

source.text: Καὶ ἦσαν οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι νηστεύοντες.

records.literal_gloss: And were the disciples of John and the Pharisees fasting.

en.L: And the disciples of John and the Pharisees were fasting.
en.B: John's disciples and the Pharisees were keeping a fast.
en.R: At that time John's followers and the Pharisees were fasting. They went without food for a time to worship God.

vi.L: Và các môn đồ của Giăng và những người Pha-ri-si đang kiêng ăn.
vi.B: Lúc ấy, các môn đồ của Giăng và những người Pha-ri-si đang giữ kỳ kiêng ăn.
vi.R: Lúc đó, các môn đồ của Giăng và những người Pha-ri-si đang kiêng ăn, tức là nhịn ăn một thời gian để thờ phượng Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: 그리고 요한의 제자들과 바리새파 사람들이 금식하고 있었다.
ko.B: 그때 요한의 제자들과 바리새파 사람들은 금식을 하고 있었다.
ko.R: 그 무렵 요한의 제자들과 바리새파 사람들은 금식을 하고 있었다. 그들은 하나님을 섬기는 뜻으로 얼마 동안 음식을 먹지 않았다.

es.L: Y los discípulos de Juan y los fariseos estaban ayunando.
es.B: Los discípulos de Juan y los fariseos estaban guardando un ayuno.
es.R: En ese tiempo, los discípulos de Juan y los fariseos estaban ayunando. Pasaban un tiempo sin comer para adorar a Dios.

fr.L: Et les disciples de Jean et les Pharisiens étaient en train de jeûner.
fr.B: Les disciples de Jean et les Pharisiens observaient un jeûne.
fr.R: À ce moment-là, les disciples de Jean et les Pharisiens jeûnaient. Ils se privaient de nourriture pendant un temps pour adorer Dieu.

sw.L: Na wanafunzi wa Yohana na Mafarisayo walikuwa wanafunga.
sw.B: Wanafunzi wa Yohana na Mafarisayo walikuwa wakishika mfungo.
sw.R: Wakati huo wanafunzi wa Yohana na Mafarisayo walikuwa wakifunga. Waliacha kula chakula kwa muda ili kumwabudu Mungu.

decisions.choice: fasting: going without food as a religious act
decisions.reason: The law set one fast a year, on the Day of Atonement. Pharisees also fasted twice a week (Luke 18:12). Fasting went with prayer, mourning and repentance.

decisions.choice: were fasting: they were keeping a fast at the time
decisions.reason: The words may describe a fast going on that day, or their regular practice.

decisions.choice: went without food for a time to worship God
decisions.reason: Readable explains what fasting is.

decisions.choice: "kiêng ăn" for fasting
decisions.reason: "ăn chay" today means eating no meat, a different practice; "kiêng ăn" is the Protestant word for going without food. Readable explains it once with "nhịn ăn".

decisions.choice: "금식" at every level
decisions.reason: "금식" is the word for going without food as a religious act; "단식" suggests a hunger strike or a diet. Readable explains it once, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ἔρχονται καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Διὰ τί οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ τῶν Φαρισαίων νηστεύουσιν, οἱ δὲ σοὶ μαθηταὶ οὐ νηστεύουσιν;

records.literal_gloss: And they come and say to him, Because of why the disciples of John and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but the your disciples not fast?

en.L: And they come and say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Why do the disciples of John and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples do not fast?"
en.B: People came and asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "John's disciples fast, and so do the Pharisees' disciples. Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples not fast?"
en.R: Some people came to Jesus and asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "John's followers and the Pharisees' followers fast. Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} followers not fast?"

vi.L: Và người ta đến và nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Tại sao các môn đồ của Giăng và các môn đồ của người Pha-ri-si kiêng ăn, còn các môn đồ của Thầy không kiêng ăn?"
vi.B: Có người đến hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Các môn đồ của Giăng và các môn đồ của người Pha-ri-si đều kiêng ăn. Sao các môn đồ của Thầy lại không kiêng ăn?"
vi.R: Có mấy người đến hỏi Đức Giê-xu: "Các môn đồ của Giăng và các môn đồ của người Pha-ri-si đều kiêng ăn. Tại sao các môn đồ của Thầy không kiêng ăn?"

ko.L: 그리고 [사람들이] 와서 그분께 말씀드린다. "요한의 제자들과 바리새파 사람들의 제자들은 금식하는데, 어찌하여 선생님의 제자들은 금식하지 않습니까?"
ko.B: 사람들이 예수께 와서 물었다. "요한의 제자들도 금식하고 바리새파 사람들의 제자들도 금식합니다. 그런데 왜 선생님의 제자들은 금식하지 않습니까?"
ko.R: 몇몇 사람이 예수께 와서 물었다. "요한의 제자들과 바리새파 사람들의 제자들은 금식합니다. 그런데 왜 선생님의 제자들은 금식하지 않습니까?"

es.L: Y vienen y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dicen: «¿Por qué los discípulos de Juan y los discípulos de los fariseos ayunan, pero {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos no ayunan?».
es.B: Algunos se acercaron y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron: «Los discípulos de Juan ayunan, y también los de los fariseos. ¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos no ayunan?».
es.R: Algunas personas se acercaron a Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron: «Los discípulos de Juan y los discípulos de los fariseos ayunan. ¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos no ayunan?».

fr.L: Et ils viennent et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} disent : « Pourquoi les disciples de Jean et les disciples des Pharisiens jeûnent-ils, mais {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} disciples ne jeûnent pas ? »
fr.B: Des gens vinrent {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demander : « Les disciples de Jean jeûnent, et ceux des Pharisiens aussi. Pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} disciples ne jeûnent-ils pas ? »
fr.R: Des gens sont venus demander à Jésus : « Les disciples de Jean et les disciples des Pharisiens jeûnent. Pourquoi est-ce que {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} disciples ne jeûnent pas ? »

sw.L: Na wanakuja na kumwambia, "Kwa nini wanafunzi wa Yohana na wanafunzi wa Mafarisayo wanafunga, lakini wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} hawafungi?"
sw.B: Watu fulani wakaja, wakamwuliza, "Wanafunzi wa Yohana hufunga, na wanafunzi wa Mafarisayo pia hufunga. Kwa nini wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} hawafungi?"
sw.R: Watu fulani walimjia Yesu, wakamwuliza, "Wanafunzi wa Yohana na wanafunzi wa Mafarisayo hufunga. Kwa nini wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} hawafungi?"

decisions.choice: they come: some people, not named
decisions.reason: Mark does not say who asked. Matthew 9:14 says it was John's disciples.

decisions.choice: your disciples: a teacher was answerable for his disciples
decisions.reason: The question is about the disciples, but it tests the teacher who trains them.

decisions.choice: the questioners call Jesus "Thầy", with no setting span
decisions.reason: They ask him as a teacher answerable for his disciples (meaning decision), and are not shown as opponents, so they use the respectful noun of address the style guide allows to others who respect him.

decisions.choice: people speak to Jesus in 합쇼체, with "선생님의" for "your"; "[사람들이]" (L)
decisions.reason: As the style guide and Mark 1:37: people address Jesus formally, and a title replaces the pronoun "you". Korean needs a subject for "they come", which the Greek leaves unnamed (meaning decision), so Literal brackets it.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ δύνανται οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ νυμφῶνος ἐν ᾧ ὁ νυμφίος μετ’ αὐτῶν ἐστιν νηστεύειν;

records.literal_gloss: And said to them the Jesus, Not are able the sons of the bridal chamber while the bridegroom with them is to fast?

en.L: And Jesus said to them, "The sons of the bridal chamber cannot fast while the bridegroom is with them, can they?
en.B: Jesus answered, "Can the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is there with them?
en.R: Jesus said to them, "When there is a wedding, the groom's friends do not go without food while he is with them.

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Các con trai của phòng cưới có thể kiêng ăn trong khi chàng rể còn ở với họ sao?
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Khách dự tiệc cưới có thể kiêng ăn khi chàng rể còn ở với họ không?
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Khi có đám cưới, bạn bè của chàng rể không kiêng ăn trong lúc chàng rể còn ở với họ.
