ko.L: 그러자 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "신랑이 그들과 함께 있는 동안에 신방의 아들들이 금식할 수 있겠느냐?
ko.B: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "신랑이 함께 있는 동안에 혼인 잔치의 손님들이 금식할 수 있겠느냐?
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "결혼 잔치가 열리면, 신랑의 친구들은 신랑이 함께 있는 동안 금식하지 않는다.

es.L: Y Jesús les dijo: «¿Acaso pueden ayunar los hijos de la cámara nupcial mientras el novio está con ellos?
es.B: Jesús les respondió: «¿Pueden acaso ayunar los invitados de la boda mientras el novio está con ellos?
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «Cuando hay una boda, los amigos del novio no dejan de comer mientras él está con ellos.

fr.L: Et Jésus leur dit : « Les fils de la chambre nuptiale peuvent-ils jeûner pendant que l’époux est avec eux ?
fr.B: Jésus leur répondit : « Les invités de la noce peuvent-ils jeûner pendant que le marié est avec eux ?
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Pendant un mariage, les amis du marié ne se privent pas de manger tant que le marié est avec eux.

sw.L: Na Yesu akawaambia, "Wana wa chumba cha harusi hawawezi kufunga bwana harusi akiwa pamoja nao, sivyo?
sw.B: Yesu akawajibu, "Je, wageni wa harusi wanaweza kufunga wakati bwana harusi yupo pamoja nao?
sw.R: Yesu akawaambia, "Kunapokuwa na harusi, rafiki za bwana harusi hawaachi kula wakati yeye yuko pamoja nao.

decisions.choice: the sons of the bridal chamber: the groom's friends and guests at the wedding
decisions.reason: The Semitic phrase "sons of" means those who belong to something. Here they are the bridegroom's attendants and guests.

decisions.choice: the bridegroom: a wedding was a week of feasting and joy
decisions.reason: No one fasted at a wedding. The guests ate and celebrated with the groom.

decisions.choice: the bridegroom: Jesus speaks of himself
decisions.reason: The prophets pictured God as Israel's husband (Hosea 2:19-20; Isaiah 62:5). Jesus speaks of himself as the bridegroom, and his time with his disciples as a wedding.

decisions.choice: cannot ... can they? a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The Greek form expects "no".

decisions.choice: a statement (R)
decisions.reason: Readable states the answer the question expects.

decisions.choice: "các con trai của phòng cưới" (L); "khách dự tiệc cưới" (B); "bạn bè của chàng rể" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew-style idiom so the reader sees it; Balanced and Readable say who is meant, the guests and the groom's friends (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "신방의 아들들" (L); "혼인 잔치의 손님들" (B); "신랑의 친구들" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom "sons of the bridal chamber"; Balanced and Readable say who they are, the groom's friends and guests (meaning decision). "혼인 잔치" and "결혼 잔치" follow John 2:1 in Korean. The ending "-겠느냐" carries the expected answer no.

decisions.choice: ¿Acaso pueden ...? (L); ¿Pueden acaso ...? (B)
decisions.reason: Spanish "acaso" marks a question that expects the answer no (meaning decision m4), which English does with "can they?".

decisions.choice: él, no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The pronoun is for the bridegroom in the picture, not for Jesus directly, so it takes no setting (English style guide, section 6).

decisions.choice: les fils de la chambre nuptiale, l’époux (L); les invités de la noce, le marié (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew-style idiom (meaning decision m1) and the older word "époux"; Balanced and Readable say "le marié", the word French uses for a man on his wedding day. The bridegroom is a figure in a picture, so, as in English, no deity_pronoun span goes on "eux" or "le marié" (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: bwana harusi
decisions.reason: "Harusi" is the usual modern spelling in Tanzania and Kenya; the older "arusi" is now mostly found in Bibles. The groom is "bwana harusi" at every level, and in this saying "yeye" for him takes no deity_pronoun span, since it is a figure in a picture.

source.text: ὅσον χρόνον ἔχουσιν τὸν νυμφίον μετ’ αὐτῶν οὐ δύνανται νηστεύειν·

records.literal_gloss: As long as time they have the bridegroom with them, not they are able to fast.

en.L: As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they are not able to fast.
en.B: As long as they have the bridegroom with them, fasting is out of the question.
en.R: As long as the groom is there, they cannot fast.

vi.L: Bao lâu họ còn có chàng rể ở với mình, họ không thể kiêng ăn.
vi.B: Bao lâu chàng rể còn ở với họ, họ không thể nào kiêng ăn được.
vi.R: Khi chàng rể còn ở đó, họ không thể kiêng ăn.

ko.L: 그들이 신랑을 자기들과 함께 두고 있는 동안에는 금식할 수 없다.
ko.B: 신랑과 함께 있는 한, 그들은 금식할 수 없다.
ko.R: 신랑이 함께 있는 동안에는 금식할 수 없다.

es.L: Todo el tiempo que tienen al novio con ellos, no pueden ayunar.
es.B: Mientras tengan con ellos al novio, no tiene sentido que ayunen.
es.R: Mientras el novio está allí, no pueden ayunar.

fr.L: Aussi longtemps qu’ils ont l’époux avec eux, ils ne peuvent pas jeûner.
fr.B: Tant qu’ils ont le marié avec eux, il n’est pas question qu’ils jeûnent.
fr.R: Tant que le marié est là, ils ne peuvent pas jeûner.

sw.L: Kwa muda wote walio na bwana harusi pamoja nao, hawawezi kufunga.
sw.B: Maadamu bwana harusi yuko pamoja nao, hawawezi kufunga hata kidogo.
sw.R: Kwa muda wote bwana harusi akiwa pamoja nao, hawawezi kufunga.

decisions.choice: the answer to the question: they cannot fast
decisions.reason: Jesus answers his own question. Fasting is for mourning, not for a time of joy.

source.text: ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος, καὶ τότε νηστεύσουσιν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: Will come but days when will be taken away from them the bridegroom, and then they will fast in that the day.

en.L: But days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast on that day.
en.B: But days are coming when the bridegroom will be taken from them; on that day they will fast.
en.R: But a day is coming when the groom will be taken away from them. Then they will fast.

vi.L: Nhưng sẽ có những ngày khi chàng rể bị đem đi khỏi họ, và bấy giờ họ sẽ kiêng ăn trong ngày ấy.
vi.B: Nhưng sẽ đến những ngày chàng rể bị đem đi khỏi họ; trong ngày ấy họ sẽ kiêng ăn.
vi.R: Nhưng sẽ đến ngày chàng rể bị đem đi khỏi họ. Lúc đó họ sẽ kiêng ăn.

ko.L: 그러나 그들이 신랑을 빼앗길 날들이 올 것이다. 그리고 그때에, 그날에 그들이 금식할 것이다.
ko.B: 그러나 신랑이 그들에게서 끌려갈 날들이 올 것이다. 그날이 되면 그들은 금식할 것이다.
ko.R: 그러나 신랑이 그들 곁에서 끌려가는 날이 올 것이다. 그때가 되면 그들은 금식할 것이다.

es.L: Pero vendrán días cuando el novio les será quitado, y entonces ayunarán en aquel día.
es.B: Pero llegarán días en que el novio les será quitado; ese día sí ayunarán.
es.R: Pero llegará un día en que se llevarán al novio lejos de ellos. Entonces sí ayunarán.

fr.L: Mais des jours viendront où l’époux leur sera enlevé, et alors ils jeûneront en ce jour-là.
fr.B: Mais un temps viendra où le marié leur sera enlevé : ce jour-là, ils jeûneront.
fr.R: Mais un jour viendra où on leur enlèvera le marié. Alors, ils jeûneront.

sw.L: Lakini siku zitakuja ambapo bwana harusi ataondolewa kutoka kwao, na hapo watafunga siku ile.
sw.B: Lakini siku zinakuja ambapo bwana harusi ataondolewa kwao; siku hiyo watafunga.
sw.R: Lakini siku moja bwana harusi atachukuliwa kutoka kwao. Wakati huo watafunga.

decisions.choice: taken away: the first hint of Jesus' death
alternatives: the bridegroom leaves on a journey
decisions.reason: The groom does not leave; he is taken. The verb suggests force and loss. Jesus will speak openly of his death from 8:31.

decisions.choice: on that day: the day he is taken, and the time after it
decisions.reason: Mark has "that day" in the singular after "days" in the plural. Then his disciples will mourn and fast.

decisions.choice: "빼앗기다" (L); "끌려가다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The passive "is taken away" is the first hint of Jesus' death (meaning decision); "빼앗기다" and "끌려가다" keep the sense that he is taken by force, which "떠나가다" (go away) would lose.

source.text: Οὐδεὶς ἐπίβλημα ῥάκους ἀγνάφου ἐπιράπτει ἐπὶ ἱμάτιον παλαιόν· εἰ δὲ μή, αἴρει τὸ πλήρωμα ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ τὸ καινὸν τοῦ παλαιοῦ, καὶ χεῖρον σχίσμα γίνεται.

records.literal_gloss: No one a patch of cloth unshrunk sews on garment old; if but not, takes away the filling from it, the new from the old, and worse a tear becomes.

en.L: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; otherwise the patch pulls away from it, the new from the old, and a worse tear is made.
en.B: Nobody sews a piece of new, unshrunk cloth onto an old coat. If they did, the new patch would shrink and tear away from the old cloth, and the hole would get worse.
en.R: People do not use new cloth to fix a hole in old clothes. The new cloth will shrink when it gets wet, and it will tear away from the old cloth. Then the hole will be bigger.

vi.L: Không ai vá một miếng vải chưa co lên áo cũ; nếu không, miếng vá sẽ kéo rời khỏi nó, cái mới khỏi cái cũ, và chỗ rách càng tệ hơn.
vi.B: Không ai lấy miếng vải mới chưa co để vá áo cũ. Nếu làm vậy, miếng vá mới sẽ co lại và kéo rách vải cũ, làm chỗ rách càng lớn hơn.
vi.R: Người ta không lấy vải mới để vá chỗ rách trên áo cũ. Vải mới gặp nước sẽ co lại và kéo rách vải cũ. Rồi chỗ rách sẽ còn lớn hơn.

ko.L: 아무도 빨지 않은 천의 조각을 낡은 옷에 대고 깁지 않는다. 그렇지 않으면 채워 댄 것이 그 옷에서, 곧 새것이 낡은 것에서 떨어져 나가고, 더 심하게 찢어진다.
ko.B: 아무도 물에 빨지 않은 새 천 조각을 낡은 옷에 대고 깁지 않는다. 그렇게 하면 새 조각이 줄어들면서 낡은 옷을 당겨 떨어져 나가고, 구멍이 더 커진다.
ko.R: 사람들은 헌 옷에 난 구멍을 새 천으로 메우지 않는다. 새 천은 물에 젖으면 줄어들어서 헌 옷에서 찢겨 나간다. 그러면 구멍이 더 커진다.

es.L: Nadie cose un remiendo de tela sin encoger en un vestido viejo; de lo contrario, el remiendo tira de él, lo nuevo de lo viejo, y se hace peor la rotura.
es.B: Nadie le cose un remiendo de tela nueva, sin encoger, a un manto viejo. Si lo hiciera, el remiendo nuevo encogería y se desprendería de la tela vieja, y la rotura se haría peor.
es.R: Nadie usa tela nueva para tapar un agujero en ropa vieja. La tela nueva se encoge cuando se moja, y se desprende de la tela vieja. Entonces el agujero se hace más grande.

fr.L: Personne ne coud une pièce d’étoffe non rétrécie sur un vieux vêtement ; sinon, la pièce se détache de lui, le neuf du vieux, et la déchirure devient pire.
fr.B: Personne ne coud un morceau de tissu neuf, qui n’a pas encore rétréci, sur un vieux manteau. Sinon, la pièce neuve rétrécit et arrache le vieux tissu, et le trou s’agrandit.
fr.R: On ne prend pas du tissu neuf pour réparer un trou dans un vieux vêtement. Quand il est mouillé, le tissu neuf rétrécit, et il arrache le vieux tissu. Alors le trou devient plus grand.

sw.L: Hakuna mtu anayeshona kiraka cha kitambaa ambacho hakijafuliwa kwenye vazi kuukuu; la sivyo, kiraka hicho huvutika kutoka kwake, kipya kutoka kwa kikuukuu, na mpasuko unakuwa mbaya zaidi.
sw.B: Hakuna mtu anayeshona kiraka cha kitambaa kipya ambacho hakijafuliwa kwenye koti kuukuu. Akifanya hivyo, kiraka kipya kitasinyaa na kuchanika kutoka kwenye kitambaa kikuukuu, na tundu litazidi kuwa baya.
sw.R: Watu hawatumii kitambaa kipya kushona tundu katika nguo kuukuu. Kitambaa kipya kitasinyaa kikiloana, nacho kitachanika kutoka kwenye kitambaa kikuukuu. Kisha tundu litakuwa kubwa zaidi.

decisions.choice: unshrunk cloth: new woolen cloth that has not yet been washed
decisions.reason: New cloth shrinks the first time it is washed. Sewn onto an old garment, it pulls and tears it.

decisions.choice: the new and the old do not mix: what Jesus brings cannot be added to old ways
decisions.reason: The picture answers the question about fasting: the new time that has come with Jesus does not fit into old practices.

decisions.choice: shrink (B); shrink when it gets wet (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say why the patch pulls away, which the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: "빨지 않은 천" (L); "물에 빨지 않은 새 천" (B)
decisions.reason: The cloth is new woollen cloth not yet washed, so it will shrink (meaning decision); "생베" is the older Bible word and names hemp cloth.

decisions.choice: non rétrécie (L)
decisions.reason: New woollen cloth that has not yet been washed (meaning decision m1). The cloth-maker's term "non foulée" is exact but few readers know it; "non rétrécie" says what matters for the saying.

source.text: καὶ οὐδεὶς βάλλει οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς· εἰ δὲ μή, ῥήξει ὁ οἶνος τοὺς ἀσκούς, καὶ ὁ οἶνος ἀπόλλυται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοί.

records.literal_gloss: And no one puts wine new into wineskins old; if but not, will burst the wine the skins, and the wine is lost and the skins.

en.L: And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wine will burst the skins, and the wine is lost, and the skins [too].
en.B: And nobody pours new wine into old wineskins. If they did, the wine would split the skins, and both wine and skins would be lost.
en.R: And people do not put new wine into old bags made of skin. The new wine would make the old bags burst, and the wine and the bags would both be lost.

vi.L: Và không ai đổ rượu mới vào bầu da cũ; nếu không, rượu sẽ làm nứt bầu, và rượu mất, và bầu [cũng mất].
vi.B: Cũng không ai đổ rượu mới vào bầu da cũ. Nếu làm vậy, rượu sẽ làm bục bầu da, và cả rượu lẫn bầu đều hư mất.
vi.R: Người ta cũng không đổ rượu mới vào túi da cũ. Rượu mới sẽ làm túi da cũ bị vỡ, rồi cả rượu lẫn túi đều bị mất.

ko.L: 그리고 아무도 새 포도주를 낡은 가죽 부대에 넣지 않는다. 그렇지 않으면 포도주가 가죽 부대를 터뜨려서, 포도주도 없어지고 부대도 [없어진다].
ko.B: 또 아무도 새 포도주를 낡은 가죽 부대에 담지 않는다. 그렇게 하면 포도주가 부대를 터뜨려서, 포도주와 부대를 둘 다 잃게 된다.
ko.R: 또 사람들은 새 포도주를 짐승 가죽으로 만든 낡은 부대에 담지 않는다. 새 포도주가 낡은 부대를 터뜨려서, 포도주도 쏟아지고 부대도 못 쓰게 되기 때문이다.

es.L: Y nadie echa vino nuevo en odres viejos; de lo contrario, el vino romperá los odres, y se pierden el vino y los odres.
es.B: Y nadie echa vino nuevo en odres viejos. Si lo hiciera, el vino reventaría los odres, y se perderían tanto el vino como los odres.
es.R: Y nadie pone vino nuevo en bolsas viejas hechas de cuero. El vino nuevo haría reventar las bolsas viejas, y se perderían el vino y las bolsas.

fr.L: Et personne ne met du vin nouveau dans de vieilles outres ; sinon, le vin fera éclater les outres, et le vin est perdu, et les outres [aussi].
fr.B: Et personne ne verse du vin nouveau dans de vieilles outres. Sinon, le vin fait éclater les outres, et l’on perd à la fois le vin et les outres.
fr.R: On ne met pas non plus du vin nouveau dans de vieux sacs en peau. Le vin nouveau ferait éclater les vieux sacs, et on perdrait à la fois le vin et les sacs.

sw.L: Na hakuna mtu amiminaye divai mpya ndani ya viriba vya zamani; akifanya hivyo, divai itavipasua viriba, nayo divai inapotea, na viriba [pia].
sw.B: Wala hakuna mtu anayemimina divai mpya katika viriba vikuukuu. Akifanya hivyo, divai itavipasua viriba, na divai na viriba vyote vitapotea.
sw.R: Watu hawaweki divai mpya katika mifuko mikuukuu ya ngozi. Divai mpya ingeipasua mifuko hiyo, na divai na mifuko vyote vingepotea.

decisions.choice: wineskins: bags made of goat or sheep skin
decisions.reason: New wine was still fermenting and gave off gas. An old skin had lost its stretch and would split.

decisions.choice: the wine and the skins: both are lost
decisions.reason: The Greek ends the sentence with "and the skins", adding them to the loss.

decisions.choice: bags made of skin
decisions.reason: Readable says what a wineskin is.

decisions.choice: "bầu da" (L, B); "túi da" (R) for wineskins
decisions.reason: "bầu da" is the established word for a skin used as a container; Readable says "túi da" (leather bag), which a new reader pictures at once.

decisions.choice: odres (L, B); bolsas hechas de cuero (R)
decisions.reason: "Odre" is the Spanish word for a wineskin (meaning decision m1); Readable says what it was, as the English does.

decisions.choice: viriba (L, B); mifuko ya ngozi (R)
alternatives: mifuko ya ngozi at every level
decisions.reason: "Kiriba" (plural "viriba") is the Swahili word for a skin bag for water or wine, which is what a wineskin was (meaning decision); Readable says "bags of skin", as the English Readable does.

source.text: ἀλλὰ οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς καινούς.

records.literal_gloss: But wine new into wineskins new.

en.L: But new wine [goes] into new wineskins.
en.B: New wine needs new skins.
en.R: New wine must be put into new bags.

vi.L: Nhưng rượu mới [thì đổ] vào bầu da mới.
vi.B: Rượu mới phải đựng trong bầu da mới.
vi.R: Rượu mới phải được đổ vào túi da mới.

ko.L: 오히려 새 포도주는 새 가죽 부대에 [넣는다]."
ko.B: 새 포도주는 새 부대에 담아야 한다."
ko.R: 새 포도주는 반드시 새 부대에 담아야 한다."

es.L: Sino [que] vino nuevo [se echa] en odres nuevos.
es.B: El vino nuevo necesita odres nuevos.
es.R: El vino nuevo se tiene que poner en bolsas nuevas.

fr.L: Mais du vin nouveau dans des outres neuves. »
fr.B: À vin nouveau, outres neuves ! »
fr.R: Le vin nouveau, il faut le mettre dans des sacs neufs. »

sw.L: Lakini divai mpya [huwekwa] ndani ya viriba vipya.
sw.B: Divai mpya inahitaji viriba vipya.
sw.R: Divai mpya lazima iwekwe katika mifuko mipya.

decisions.choice: no verb: a short saying
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves out the verb, as a proverb does.

decisions.choice: new: new in age (the wine) and fresh (the skins)
decisions.reason: The two Greek words for new differ slightly; the first means young, the second fresh and unused.

decisions.choice: [goes]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies a verb in brackets.

decisions.choice: no verb (L); À vin nouveau, outres neuves (B)
alternatives: Le vin nouveau se met dans des outres neuves
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb, a short saying (meaning decision m1). French can leave the verb out too, so Literal needs no bracket, and Balanced takes the shape of a French proverb ("à ... , ..."). Jesus's answer, opened in 2:19, closes here at every level.

source.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο αὐτὸν ἐν τοῖς σάββασιν παραπορεύεσθαι διὰ τῶν σπορίμων, καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἤρξαντο ὁδὸν ποιεῖν τίλλοντες τοὺς στάχυας.

records.literal_gloss: And it came to pass he on the Sabbaths to pass through the grainfields, and the disciples of him began a way to make plucking the heads of grain.

en.L: And it happened that on the Sabbath {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was passing through the grainfields, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples began to make [their] way, plucking the heads of grain.
en.B: One Sabbath Jesus was going through the grainfields, and as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples made their way along, they started to pick heads of grain.
en.R: One Sabbath day, Jesus was walking through some fields of grain with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers. As they walked, they picked some of the grain to eat.

vi.L: Và xảy ra là vào ngày Sa-bát {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi ngang qua các đồng lúa, và các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vừa đi đường vừa bắt đầu bứt các bông lúa.
vi.B: Một ngày Sa-bát, Đức Giê-xu đi ngang qua các đồng lúa. Khi đi đường, các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bắt đầu bứt bông lúa.
vi.R: Vào một ngày Sa-bát, Đức Giê-xu cùng các môn đồ đi ngang qua mấy đồng lúa. Vừa đi, các môn đồ vừa bứt bông lúa để ăn.

ko.L: 그리고 안식일에 그분이 곡식밭 사이로 지나가시게 되었다. 그리고 그분의 제자들은 길을 가면서 이삭을 따기 시작했다.
ko.B: 어느 안식일에 예수께서 곡식밭 사이로 지나가고 계셨다. 제자들은 길을 따라가면서 이삭을 따기 시작했다.
ko.R: 어느 안식일에 예수께서 제자들과 함께 곡식밭 사이로 걸어가고 계셨다. 제자들은 걸어가면서 먹으려고 곡식 이삭을 땄다.

es.L: Y sucedió que en sábado pasaba {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} por los sembrados, y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos comenzaron a abrir camino arrancando las espigas.
es.B: Un sábado, Jesús pasaba por los sembrados, y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, mientras caminaban, comenzaron a arrancar espigas.
es.R: Un sábado, Jesús caminaba con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos por unos sembrados. Mientras caminaban, arrancaron algunas espigas para comer.

fr.L: Et il arriva qu’un jour de sabbat {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} passait à travers les champs de blé, et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples commencèrent à faire route en arrachant les épis.
fr.B: Un jour de sabbat, Jésus traversait des champs de blé, et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples, chemin faisant, se mirent à cueillir des épis.
fr.R: Un jour de sabbat, Jésus marchait à travers des champs de blé avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples. En marchant, les disciples ont cueilli des épis pour manger les grains.

sw.L: Na ikawa siku ya Sabato {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} akipita katikati ya mashamba ya nafaka, na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakaanza kufanya njia [yao], wakichuma masuke.
sw.B: Siku moja ya Sabato Yesu alikuwa akipita katika mashamba ya nafaka, na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walipokuwa wakitembea, wakaanza kuchuma masuke.
sw.R: Siku moja ya Sabato, Yesu alikuwa akitembea katika mashamba ya nafaka pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Walipokuwa wakitembea, walichuma masuke ya nafaka ili wale.

decisions.choice: make their way: walk along a path
alternatives: make a path by trampling the grain
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean making a road, but here it most likely means going along the path while they picked.

decisions.choice: plucking heads of grain: allowed on any day in a neighbor's field
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 23:25 lets a traveler pick grain by hand from a neighbor's field. The question is not taking the grain but doing it on the Sabbath (2:24).

decisions.choice: on the Sabbaths: on a Sabbath day
decisions.reason: As in 1:21, the plural names a single Sabbath.

decisions.choice: to eat
decisions.reason: Readable says why they picked it, which 2:25 makes clear: they were hungry.

decisions.choice: "đồng lúa", "bông lúa" for the grainfields and heads of grain
decisions.reason: The crop was wheat or barley; "lúa" is used in the general sense of grain, while "lúa mì" would name only wheat and "ruộng" suggests wet rice paddies. A reviewer may judge whether "lúa" reads as rice.

decisions.choice: "곡식밭"
decisions.reason: The Greek word means sown fields of grain without naming the crop; "곡식밭" keeps it general.

decisions.choice: sábado
decisions.reason: The Jewish day of rest, written lower-case as in John 19:31 and Colossians 2:16. Throughout Mark.

decisions.choice: faire route (L)
decisions.reason: "Faire route" is the French idiom for walking along a way (meaning decision m1), so Literal needs no bracket; "se frayer un chemin" would suggest pushing through the crop.

source.text: καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἔλεγον αὐτῷ· Ἴδε τί ποιοῦσιν τοῖς σάββασιν ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν;

records.literal_gloss: And the Pharisees were saying to him, Look, why do they on the Sabbaths what not is lawful?

en.L: And the Pharisees were saying to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Look, why are they doing on the Sabbath what is not lawful?"
en.B: The Pharisees said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "See there! Why are they doing something on the Sabbath that the law forbids?"
en.R: The Pharisees said to Jesus, "Look! Your followers are breaking the Sabbath law. Why are they doing that?"

vi.L: Và những người Pha-ri-si nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Kìa, sao họ làm điều không được phép trong ngày Sa-bát?"
vi.B: Những người Pha-ri-si nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ông xem kìa! Sao họ lại làm điều luật pháp cấm trong ngày Sa-bát?"
vi.R: Những người Pha-ri-si nói với Đức Giê-xu: "Ông xem kìa! Môn đồ của ông đang vi phạm luật ngày Sa-bát. Sao họ lại làm như vậy?"

ko.L: 그리고 바리새파 사람들이 그분께 말하고 있었다. "보십시오, 어찌하여 저들이 안식일에 해서는 안 되는 일을 합니까?"
ko.B: 바리새파 사람들이 예수께 말했다. "보십시오! 저 사람들이 왜 안식일에 율법이 금하는 일을 합니까?"
ko.R: 바리새파 사람들이 예수께 말했다. "보십시오! 선생님의 제자들이 안식일 법을 어기고 있습니다. 왜 저런 일을 합니까?"

es.L: Y los fariseos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} decían: «Mira, ¿por qué hacen en sábado lo que no es lícito?».
es.B: Los fariseos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «¡Mira! ¿Por qué hacen en sábado algo que la ley prohíbe?».
es.R: Los fariseos dijeron a Jesús: «¡Mira! Tus discípulos están quebrantando la ley del sábado. ¿Por qué hacen eso?».

fr.L: Et les Pharisiens {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} disaient : « Regarde, pourquoi font-ils le jour du sabbat ce qui n’est pas permis ? »
fr.B: Les Pharisiens {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent : « Vois donc ! Pourquoi font-ils, le jour du sabbat, ce que la Loi interdit ? »
fr.R: Les Pharisiens ont dit à Jésus : « Regarde ! Tes disciples désobéissent à la loi du sabbat. Pourquoi font-ils cela ? »

sw.L: Na Mafarisayo walikuwa wakimwambia, "Angalia, kwa nini siku ya Sabato wanafanya jambo lisilo halali?"
sw.B: Mafarisayo wakamwambia, "Tazama! Kwa nini wanafanya siku ya Sabato jambo ambalo sheria inakataza?"
sw.R: Mafarisayo wakamwambia Yesu, "Angalia! Wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wanavunja sheria ya Sabato. Kwa nini wanafanya hivyo?"

decisions.choice: not lawful: they counted plucking grain as reaping, work forbidden on the Sabbath
decisions.reason: The law forbids work on the Sabbath, even at harvest (Exodus 34:21). The Pharisees' teaching counted plucking grain as reaping.

decisions.choice: to him: the teacher is held responsible for his disciples
alternatives: the Pharisees speak to the disciples
decisions.reason: As in 2:18, the complaint about the disciples is brought to Jesus.

decisions.choice: a statement, then why (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the complaint is before asking why.

decisions.choice: the Pharisees call Jesus "ông"
decisions.reason: Opponents do not call him Teacher; "ông" is polite but keeps their distance, as the style guide sets for those who do not believe.

decisions.choice: the Pharisees address Jesus in 합쇼체 ("보십시오", "합니까")
decisions.reason: Their challenge is in what they say, not in open contempt, so the style guide's default for people speaking to Jesus holds, as for the accusers in John 8:4-5 in Korean.

source.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Οὐδέποτε ἀνέγνωτε τί ἐποίησεν Δαυὶδ ὅτε χρείαν ἔσχεν καὶ ἐπείνασεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ;

records.literal_gloss: And he says to them, Never did you read what did David when need he had and was hungry, he and those with him?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Have you never read what David did when he had need and was hungry, he and those with him?
en.B: He answered, "Have you not read what David did when he and his men were in need and hungry?
en.R: Jesus answered, "You have read in the Scriptures what David did when he and the men with him were hungry and had nothing to eat.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Các người chưa bao giờ đọc điều Đa-vít đã làm khi ông thiếu thốn và đói, ông và những người theo ông sao?
vi.B: Ngài đáp: "Các người chưa đọc việc Đa-vít đã làm khi ông và những người theo ông thiếu thốn và đói khát sao?
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Các người đã đọc trong Kinh Thánh việc Đa-vít đã làm khi ông và những người đi theo ông bị đói và không có gì ăn.

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 그들에게 말씀하신다. "너희는 다윗이 궁핍하여 굶주렸을 때, 곧 그와 그와 함께 있던 이들이 [굶주렸을 때], 무엇을 했는지 한 번도 읽지 못했느냐?
ko.B: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "다윗과 그 일행이 먹을 것이 없어 배고팠을 때 다윗이 어떻게 했는지 너희는 읽어 보지 못했느냐?
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "너희는 성경에서 다윗이 한 일을 읽었다. 다윗과 그와 함께 있던 사람들은 먹을 것이 없어서 배가 고팠다.

es.L: Y les dice: «¿Nunca {{plural_you:leyeron|leísteis}} lo que hizo David cuando tuvo necesidad y tuvo hambre, él y los que [estaban] con él?
es.B: Él les respondió: «¿No {{plural_you:han|habéis}} leído lo que hizo David cuando él y sus compañeros tuvieron necesidad y pasaron hambre?
es.R: Jesús les respondió: «{{plural_you:Ustedes han|Vosotros habéis}} leído en las Escrituras lo que hizo David cuando él y sus hombres tenían hambre y no tenían nada que comer.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « N’avez-vous jamais lu ce qu’a fait David lorsqu’il a été dans le besoin et qu’il a eu faim, lui et ceux qui étaient avec lui ?
fr.B: Il leur répondit : « N’avez-vous pas lu ce qu’a fait David quand il était dans le besoin et qu’il avait faim, lui et ses hommes ?
fr.R: Jésus leur a répondu : « Vous avez lu dans les Écritures ce qu’a fait David quand lui et ses hommes avaient faim et n’avaient rien à manger.

sw.L: Naye anawaambia, "Hamjawahi kusoma kile Daudi alichofanya alipokuwa katika shida na akaona njaa, yeye na wale waliokuwa pamoja naye?
sw.B: Akawajibu, "Hamjasoma kile alichofanya Daudi wakati yeye na watu wake walipokuwa na shida na njaa?
sw.R: Yesu akawajibu, "Mmesoma katika Maandiko kile Daudi alichofanya wakati yeye na watu waliokuwa pamoja naye walipokuwa na njaa, wasiwe na chakula.

decisions.choice: David: the story of 1 Samuel 21:1-6
decisions.reason: David, fleeing from Saul, came to the priest at Nob and asked for bread for himself and his men.

decisions.choice: have you never read? a rebuke to experts in the scriptures
decisions.reason: The Pharisees knew the story well. The question asks why they have not seen what it means.

decisions.choice: a statement: You have read (R)
decisions.reason: Readable states what the question assumes; the question form is kept at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: "곧 그와 그와 함께 있던 이들이 [굶주렸을 때]" (L)
alternatives: "그와 그와 함께 있던 이들이 궁핍하여 굶주렸을 때" (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek adds "he and those with him" after the verbs; Korean must put a subject before its verb, so Literal keeps the afterthought by repeating the time clause in brackets.

source.text: πῶς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ Ἀβιαθὰρ ἀρχιερέως καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως ἔφαγεν, οὓς οὐκ ἔξεστιν φαγεῖν εἰ μὴ τοὺς ἱερεῖς, καὶ ἔδωκεν καὶ τοῖς σὺν αὐτῷ οὖσιν;

records.literal_gloss: How he entered into the house of the God in [the time of] Abiathar high priest, and the loaves of the presentation he ate, which not is lawful to eat except for the priests, and he gave also to those with him being?

en.L: How he entered into the house of God in [the time of] Abiathar [the] high priest, and ate the loaves of the presentation, which it is not lawful to eat except for the priests, and he gave also to those who were with him?"
en.B: In the days of Abiathar the high priest, he went into the house of God and ate the bread set out before God, which the law allows only the priests to eat. He even gave some to the men with him."
en.R: In the time of Abiathar the high priest, David went into God's house and ate the special bread that was offered to God. The law says that only the priests may eat that bread. But David ate it, and he gave some to his men too."

vi.L: thế nào ông đã vào nhà Đức Chúa Trời vào thời A-bi-a-tha [làm] thầy tế lễ thượng phẩm, và ăn các ổ bánh bày ra [trước Đức Chúa Trời], là bánh không ai được phép ăn ngoại trừ các thầy tế lễ, và ông cũng đã cho những người ở với ông?"
vi.B: Vào thời thầy tế lễ thượng phẩm A-bi-a-tha, ông đã vào nhà Đức Chúa Trời và ăn bánh bày ra trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời, là bánh luật pháp chỉ cho phép các thầy tế lễ ăn. Ông còn đưa cho những người đi theo mình nữa."
vi.R: Vào thời A-bi-a-tha làm thầy tế lễ thượng phẩm, Đa-vít đã vào nhà của Đức Chúa Trời và ăn thứ bánh đặc biệt đã được dâng cho Đức Chúa Trời. Luật pháp nói chỉ các thầy tế lễ mới được ăn bánh đó. Nhưng Đa-vít đã ăn, và ông còn chia cho những người đi theo mình nữa."

ko.L: 대제사장 아비아달 때에 그가 어떻게 하나님의 집에 들어가서, 제사장들 말고는 먹어서는 안 되는 차려 놓은 빵을 먹고, 자기와 함께 있던 이들에게도 주었는지 [읽지 못했느냐]?"
ko.B: 대제사장 아비아달 때에, 다윗은 하나님의 집에 들어가서 하나님 앞에 차려 놓은 빵을 먹었다. 율법에 따르면 그 빵은 제사장들만 먹을 수 있었다. 그런데도 다윗은 함께 있던 사람들에게도 그 빵을 주었다."
ko.R: 아비아달이 대제사장이었을 때, 다윗은 하나님의 집에 들어가서 하나님께 바친 특별한 빵을 먹었다. 율법은 제사장들만 그 빵을 먹을 수 있다고 말한다. 그러나 다윗은 그 빵을 먹었고, 함께 있던 사람들에게도 나누어 주었다."

es.L: Cómo entró en la casa de Dios en [tiempos de] Abiatar, sumo sacerdote, y comió los panes de la presentación, que no es lícito comer sino a los sacerdotes, y dio también a los que estaban con él?».
es.B: En tiempos del sumo sacerdote Abiatar, entró en la casa de Dios y comió los panes consagrados que se ponían delante de Dios, que la ley solo permite comer a los sacerdotes. Y hasta les dio a sus compañeros».
es.R: En el tiempo en que Abiatar era sumo sacerdote, David entró en la casa de Dios y comió el pan especial que se ofrecía a Dios. La ley dice que solo los sacerdotes pueden comer ese pan. Pero David lo comió, y también les dio a sus hombres».

fr.L: Comment il est entré dans la maison de Dieu sous Abiathar, grand prêtre, et a mangé les pains de la présentation, qu’il n’est permis de manger qu’aux prêtres, et en a donné aussi à ceux qui étaient avec lui ? »
fr.B: Au temps du grand prêtre Abiathar, il est entré dans la maison de Dieu et il a mangé les pains présentés devant Dieu, que la Loi permet aux seuls prêtres de manger. Il en a même donné à ceux qui l’accompagnaient. »
fr.R: C’était à l’époque où Abiathar était grand prêtre. David est entré dans la maison de Dieu et il a mangé le pain spécial qu’on avait offert à Dieu. La Loi dit que seuls les prêtres peuvent manger ce pain. Mais David en a mangé, et il en a aussi donné à ses hommes. »

sw.L: Jinsi alivyoingia ndani ya nyumba ya Mungu katika siku za Abiathari aliyekuwa kuhani mkuu, akala mikate ya kuwekwa mbele [za Mungu], ambayo hairuhusiwi kuliwa na mtu yeyote ila makuhani, tena akawapa hata wale waliokuwa pamoja naye?"
sw.B: Katika siku za Abiathari kuhani mkuu, Daudi aliingia katika nyumba ya Mungu akala mikate iliyowekwa mbele za Mungu, ambayo sheria inaruhusu makuhani peke yao kuila. Tena aliwapa hata watu waliokuwa pamoja naye."
sw.R: Katika wakati wa Abiathari kuhani mkuu, Daudi aliingia katika nyumba ya Mungu, akala mikate maalum iliyotolewa kwa Mungu. Sheria inasema kwamba makuhani peke yao ndio wanaoweza kula mikate hiyo. Lakini Daudi aliila, na akawapa pia watu wake."

decisions.choice: the loaves of the presentation: the bread set out before God
decisions.reason: Twelve loaves were set on a table in the holy place each Sabbath and eaten by the priests the next week (Leviticus 24:5-9).

decisions.choice: in the time of Abiathar: 1 Samuel 21 names the priest Ahimelech, Abiathar's father
alternatives: Abiathar was the priest who gave the bread
decisions.reason: Abiathar was Ahimelech's son and escaped the slaughter of the priests at Nob (1 Samuel 22:20). He became David's high priest and is better known. The Greek may mean "in the time of Abiathar", or "in the passage about Abiathar", as 12:26 says "at the bush" for a passage. Some manuscripts leave out the phrase.

decisions.choice: the house of God: the tent of worship at Nob
decisions.reason: The temple was not yet built. The house of God was the tabernacle, then at Nob.

decisions.choice: David's need came before the rule
decisions.reason: Even the bread kept for the priests was given to meet human need. Jesus draws the point in 2:27.

decisions.choice: the bread set out before God (B); the special bread that was offered to God (R)
decisions.reason: Older names for the loaves are unclear today; the levels say what the bread was.

decisions.choice: "các ổ bánh bày ra" (L); "bánh bày ra trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời" (B); "thứ bánh đặc biệt đã được dâng cho Đức Chúa Trời" (R)
decisions.reason: "bánh trần thiết", the older Protestant term, is no longer understood by most readers; the plain words say what the bread was.

decisions.choice: "A-bi-a-tha" for Abiathar
decisions.reason: The Protestant transliteration; the name is not in the style guide's list.

decisions.choice: "차려 놓은 빵" (L); "하나님 앞에 차려 놓은 빵" (B); "하나님께 바친 특별한 빵" (R)
decisions.reason: "진설병" is the older church word, unknown to most readers today; the style guide says "빵" for bread, never "떡". "차려 놓다" (set out) gives the meaning of "presentation" (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "[읽지 못했느냐]" (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek "how he entered ..." continues the question "have you never read" of 2:25; Korean needs the verb at the end of the clause, so Literal repeats it in brackets.

decisions.choice: los panes de la presentación (L); los panes consagrados que se ponían delante de Dios (B); el pan especial que se ofrecía a Dios (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek phrase; Balanced and Readable say what the bread was (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: sous Abiathar, grand prêtre (L)
decisions.reason: "Sous" with a name is the French for "in the time of" someone in office, the sense of the Greek here (meaning decision m2), so Literal needs no bracket. The footnote on m2 explains the name.

decisions.choice: passé composé in Jesus's speech ("est entré", "a mangé")
decisions.reason: Jesus tells the story in speech, so every level uses the passé composé, as the French brief does for speech.

decisions.choice: mikate ya kuwekwa mbele [za Mungu] (L); mikate iliyowekwa mbele za Mungu (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek is "the loaves of the setting out", bread set out before God (meaning decision). "Mikate ya wonyesho" is the familiar older phrase, but today "wonyesho" sounds like a display or exhibition; Swahili says plainly that the bread was set before God.

source.text: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Τὸ σάββατον διὰ τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐγένετο καὶ οὐχ ὁ ἄνθρωπος διὰ τὸ σάββατον·

records.literal_gloss: And he was saying to them, The Sabbath because of the man came to be, and not the man because of the Sabbath;

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying to them, "The Sabbath came to be for the sake of {{gender:humankind|man}}, and not {{gender:humankind|man}} for the sake of the Sabbath;
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "The Sabbath was made for {{gender:people|man}}, not {{gender:people|man}} for the Sabbath.
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "God made the Sabbath to help people. He did not make people to serve the Sabbath.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Ngày Sa-bát đã được lập nên vì con người, chứ không phải con người vì ngày Sa-bát;
vi.B: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Ngày Sa-bát được lập ra vì con người, chứ không phải con người vì ngày Sa-bát.
vi.R: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Đức Chúa Trời lập ra ngày Sa-bát để giúp ích cho con người. Ngài không dựng nên con người để phục vụ ngày Sa-bát.

decisions.choice: the man: human beings
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for a human being, with the article for the whole kind. So the gender setting applies.

decisions.choice: the Sabbath was given for people's good
decisions.reason: God gave the Sabbath as rest and blessing (Exodus 20:8-11; Deuteronomy 5:12-15). Rules that turn it into a burden miss its purpose.

decisions.choice: came to be: God made it so
decisions.reason: The verb recalls creation, where God rested and blessed the seventh day (Genesis 2:2-3).

decisions.choice: God made
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who made the Sabbath, following the meaning note.

decisions.choice: "con người" with no gender span
decisions.reason: "con người" (human beings) already includes men and women; the English traditional alternative "man" has no Vietnamese counterpart that means anything different.

decisions.choice: "사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English needs a gender span for "humankind|man"; Korean "사람" already means human beings of either sex and has no traditional masculine form here, so the setting has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: {{gender:ser humano|hombre}} (L); {{gender:las personas|el hombre}} (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek word means human beings (meaning decision m1); the reader setting gives the traditional "el hombre".

decisions.choice: {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}} (L, B)
decisions.reason: The word means human beings (meaning decision m1), so, as in English, the inclusive wording is the default and the traditional "l’homme" the alternative. The article is inside the span because "l’" belongs to each word. Readable says "les gens", already inclusive, with no span.

decisions.choice: binadamu (L), watu (B, R), with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in English
decisions.reason: Swahili "binadamu" and "watu" already mean human beings, men and women, as the meaning decision reads "the man"; the only male word, "mwanamume", would change the meaning, so the gender setting has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus' name for himself
decisions.reason: As in 2:10. Some read it as "a human being", following 2:27, but in Mark it is always Jesus speaking of himself.

decisions.choice: Lord of the Sabbath: he has authority over it
alternatives: he does away with the Sabbath
decisions.reason: The Sabbath belongs to God (Exodus 20:10). Jesus claims the right to say what it is for, as in 2:10 he claims the right to forgive.

decisions.choice: so that: what follows from 2:27
decisions.reason: If the Sabbath is for human good, the Son of Man, who has authority on earth (2:10), rules over it.

decisions.choice: Lord, with a capital
decisions.reason: The word is used here of Jesus' authority over what belongs to God, so it is capitalized, as "Lord" is for Jesus elsewhere.

Jesus speaks of himself as the Son of Man, and a Korean speaker does not use the honorific "-님" of himself, so "주님" is not possible here. "주" keeps the word for Lord; Readable says "주인" (master, owner), which new readers understand as the one in charge.
